findings.description: The 20 ms limit for T_DIAG agrees with CON-SUP-103, but the configured execution limits allow 110 ms of application execution per 100 ms on the single processor if all tasks reach their limits. This excludes supervisor execution. No workload evidence establishes which execution times can occur together.
findings.requested_change: Record the schedulability question and identify the workload bounds needed to verify the configured schedule.

findings.description: CON-SUP-115 requires rejection of an unknown task. The item instead checks for a task that is not supervised, while SYS-CFG-001 defines a supervised task as one named in the configuration. An unsupported task entered into that configuration could therefore satisfy the definition used by the check.
findings.requested_change: Define the validity check against an approved set of supported task identifiers. Record an open point if that set cannot be determined from the inputs.

findings.description: The item requires the code check before supervised tasks are released. CON-SUP-107 requires the check before any task is released, and STK-SUP-007 requires it before the application runs. The current wording permits an application task outside the configured supervised set to start first.
findings.requested_change: Apply the startup code-check precondition to the release of every application task.

findings.description: CON-SUP-107 defines the image boundaries, but neither the item nor the sources define what constitutes a passing image integrity check. OP-SYS-005 records the missing method and reference value, so the stated test lacks an independent expected result.
findings.requested_change: Once the integrity decision is approved, reference the criterion and reference-value contract that the test must use.

findings.description: The item requires the configuration CRC check before supervised tasks are released. CON-SUP-107 requires the check before any task is released, and STK-SUP-007 requires it before the application runs.
findings.requested_change: Apply the startup configuration-check precondition to the release of every application task.

findings.description: The polynomial in CON-SUP-107 does not uniquely determine the stored CRC-32. OP-SYS-005 identifies missing parameters, including initialization, reflection and final XOR. The same configuration bytes can therefore yield different expected CRC values.
findings.requested_change: Reference the approved complete CRC convention and the bytes it covers so the test can compute the expected value independently.

findings.description: The item combines image coverage at startup and at runtime. A startup check can cover the complete image up to the CON-SUP-107 limit while the runtime check misses part of that same image.
findings.requested_change: Make coverage up to 1 MiB independently judgeable for the startup check and the runtime check.

findings.description: The startup release gate covers supervised tasks only. CON-SUP-107 requires the integrity checks before any task release, and STK-SUP-007 requires them before the application runs. With configurable supervision membership, the current gate leaves other application tasks free to start.
findings.requested_change: Extend the startup integrity release gate to all application tasks.

findings.description: The stated 11 s limit applies only to a 1 MiB image. STK-SUP-008 requires a bounded full pass while running, and CON-SUP-108 specifies a per-cycle segment cadence. The item leaves completion time unbounded for smaller supported images.
findings.requested_change: State a full-pass time bound for the supported image sizes using the cadence and upper bound in CON-SUP-108.

findings.description: STK-SUP-008 requires a repeat of the code integrity check. The item gives a timing criterion but lacks an approved integrity criterion and reference value. A test can time a pass without establishing that the pass recognized corrupt code.
findings.requested_change: Reference the approved integrity criterion and image reference value for the runtime check.

findings.description: The item does not identify the boundaries of the two consecutive task periods. CON-SUP-102 starts supervision when startup checks pass, while CON-SUP-105 starts the reaction clock at the end of the alive window. Measuring from startup-check completion or from the first task release can yield different fault times.
findings.requested_change: Define the first and subsequent alive-window boundaries relative to startup and task releases. Record an open point if the inputs do not establish the alignment.

findings.description: The trigger waits for a task to begin late. CON-SUP-103 defines the configured start limit, and CON-SUP-105 measures the safety reaction from expiry of a timing limit. A task that remains unstarted after expiry can defer late-start detection until it eventually runs.
findings.requested_change: Define detection when the start deadline expires without a start, including how a start exactly at the allowed limit is treated.

findings.description: The phrase 'still executing at the expiry' leaves the case where completion and expiry have the same measured timestamp open to different interpretations. CON-SUP-103 allows execution up to the configured limit and defines an overrun as execution longer than that limit.
findings.requested_change: Specify the inclusive completion boundary and the detection outcome when expiry occurs without a completion by that boundary.

findings.description: CON-SUP-103 specifies a measurement resolution of 100 µs. The item permits finer resolution without an approved rule for how finer measurements are interpreted. That choice can change fault classification near a configured timing limit.
findings.requested_change: Use the specified resolution or obtain an approved decision defining how finer measurements are used for timing-limit comparisons.

findings.description: CON-SUP-104 checks checkpoints from tasks released in the cycle, but the item does not identify what observable event constitutes a task checkpoint. This matters for T_DIAG, whose permitted execution in CON-SUP-103 can extend beyond the 10 ms cycle in CON-SUP-101.
findings.requested_change: Define or reference the observable event that supplies each task checkpoint and specify how its arrival is assigned to a control cycle.

findings.description: The control-output deadline references CON-SUP-105 for every listed fault, but that decision gives no detectability instant for the configuration-range fault in CON-SUP-115. The item supplies no start event for measuring that case.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the timing reference for configuration-range faults, including the effect of the control outputs already being low during startup under CON-SUP-109.

findings.description: The status-signal deadline references CON-SUP-105, which gives no detectability instant for the configuration-range fault in CON-SUP-115. The item supplies no start event for measuring that case.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the timing reference for configuration-range faults, including the effect of the status signal already being low during startup under CON-SUP-109.

findings.description: The item combines maintaining the control outputs with maintaining the operational status signal. STK-SUP-009 and CON-SUP-109 distinguish the two observable functions. The controller can keep the actuators off while incorrectly indicating that it is operational.
findings.requested_change: Make maintenance of the control outputs and maintenance of the status signal independently judgeable in the safe state.

findings.description: CON-SUP-109 requires both control outputs to be low from any reset. CON-SUP-003 establishes GPIO availability, but the workproduct gives no feasibility evidence or open point for maintaining both external levels during reset, before supervisor code can act.
findings.requested_change: Record the feasibility analysis needed to establish the external control-output levels throughout each supported reset path.

findings.description: CON-SUP-109 requires the status signal to be low from any reset. GPIO availability in CON-SUP-003 alone does not establish that level during reset, before supervisor code can act. The workproduct gives no feasibility analysis or open point for that interval.
findings.requested_change: Record the feasibility analysis needed to establish the external status-signal level throughout each supported reset path.

findings.description: The wording triggers reset only if a refresh actually happens outside the window. It gives no reset outcome when refreshes cease entirely, the case called for by STK-SUP-005 and treated as a window expiry in OP-SYS-004 using CON-SUP-106.
findings.requested_change: Specify the hardware reset outcome when the upper window limit expires without a refresh, including when no later refresh is attempted.

findings.description: Both this refresh and the flow check in SYS-SUP-005 occur at the end of the control cycle under CON-SUP-104 and CON-SUP-106. The item leaves their order open, so a refresh could occur in the same cycle before a flow fault is evaluated, despite the healthy-task restriction in STK-SUP-005.
findings.requested_change: Define how the end-of-cycle health decision controls the refresh for that cycle.

findings.description: The refresh condition is true whenever no listed task fault has been detected since reset. That also covers startup before supervision begins and a retained safe-state latch after reset. OP-SYS-010 records that CON-SUP-106 does not define the watchdog policy in those states.
findings.requested_change: Specify the operating states in which the periodic window-watchdog refresh is required using the approved startup and latch policy.

findings.description: The obligation to refresh at intervals shorter than 100 ms applies whenever no listed task fault has been detected since reset. This includes startup and a retained safe-state latch, where the independent-watchdog policy is undecided under OP-SYS-010.
findings.requested_change: Specify the operating states to which the independent-watchdog refresh bound applies and the approved rule for the first interval.

findings.description: Stopping refreshes on a task fault can put the CON-SUP-106 window-watchdog reset ahead of the fault report and supervisor reset required by CON-SUP-110 and CON-SUP-112. The item gives no precedence for a fault detected near window expiry.
findings.requested_change: Resolve which action takes precedence and align refresh cessation with the approved fault-report and reset sequence.

findings.description: The reset request is triggered by entering the safe state because of a fault. For a startup integrity failure, CON-SUP-109 already holds all safe-state outputs low. The item gives no clear trigger or 20 ms origin for that case, although STK-SUP-010 and CON-SUP-110 call for reset recovery.
findings.requested_change: Define the reset-request trigger and deadline origin for a qualifying fault detected while the outputs already meet the safe-state condition.

findings.description: The permitted interval of up to 20 ms after safe-state entry can extend beyond window-watchdog expiry under CON-SUP-106 when SYS-WDG-005 stops refreshes. A hardware reset can preempt the software reset request and prevent the supervisor-reset sequence in CON-SUP-110.
findings.requested_change: Define the required reset path and deadline for faults detected near watchdog expiry after the precedence decision is approved.

findings.description: CON-SUP-110 places transmission of the fault report after safe-state entry. The item constrains only transmission completion, allowing transmission to begin before the controller has entered the safe state.
findings.requested_change: Specify the ordering of safe-state entry, the start and completion of fault-report transmission, and the software reset request.

findings.description: Requiring report completion before a software reset request does not establish that the report can finish before a CON-SUP-106 hardware reset after refreshes cease. The required outcome under CON-SUP-110 is unresolved for a task fault close to watchdog expiry.
findings.requested_change: State the approved transmission outcome when the window watchdog can reset the controller during the fault-reaction sequence.

findings.description: The item uses 'consecutive supervisor reset' without defining how an intervening watchdog or other reset affects the count. It also leaves the start of the 60 s interval outside the normative text. Those choices change when the CON-SUP-110 latch is set.
findings.requested_change: Specify which intervening events break the sequence and define when the 60 s of fault-free operation begins.

findings.description: The item preserves the five classes from CON-SUP-111 but omits that classification is based on the reset flags. Its stated test could accept another basis for classification without checking the source of evidence required by CON-SUP-111.
findings.requested_change: Specify the reset flags as evidence for startup classification and identify any flag interpretation that still requires an approved reference or decision.

findings.description: CON-SUP-111 requires a startup message carrying the reset cause, but OP-SYS-002 records that its serial format is undefined. A verifier has no agreed framing or encoding for identifying the message and reading the cause.
findings.requested_change: Reference an approved startup-message format with framing and an encoding for each reset class.

findings.description: CON-SUP-111 requires the service tool to read the reset cause. CON-SUP-113 defines no response field for the cause and returns ERR for requests other than GET STATUS and GET FAULTS. The item has no approved service interaction that satisfies both decisions.
findings.requested_change: Specify the approved service request and response carrying the reset cause, and reconcile them with the ERR rule.

findings.description: CON-SUP-112 says the report is sent within 10 ms. The item does not say whether to time the first transmitted byte or completion of the terminating line feed. The rationale selects completion while OP-SYS-007 records the interpretation as undecided.
findings.requested_change: State the approved observable end event for measuring the 10 ms transmission deadline.

findings.description: The item requires a report within 10 ms for every detected fault. Under CON-SUP-106 and SYS-WDG-005, the window watchdog can reset the controller before that deadline and interrupt the report. The item gives no approved outcome for that case.
findings.requested_change: Define the report obligation when watchdog expiry can preempt transmission, using the approved reset precedence.

findings.description: SYS-DIAG-003 defines watchdog reset as fault code 8, and SYS-DIAG-002 requires an entity in every report. The item gives no entity for code 8 because the task, CODE and CONFIG values listed in CON-SUP-112 do not identify a watchdog reset.
findings.requested_change: Specify the approved entity value for a watchdog-reset fault report.

findings.description: The entity for a flow fault is 'the affected supervised task.' Under CON-SUP-104, a cycle can have multiple missing or out-of-order checkpoints. CON-SUP-112 gives no rule for which task name to report in that case.
findings.requested_change: Specify the approved task-selection and reporting rule for missing and out-of-order checkpoints, including when several checkpoints are wrong.

findings.description: CON-SUP-112 gives the field as milliseconds since start without defining the time origin. The item selects the latest reset and uses 'the controller started' without identifying an observable event. OP-SYS-007 records the time origin as undecided.
findings.requested_change: Specify the approved timestamp origin as an identifiable event and apply it to fault reports after each relevant reset type.

findings.description: STK-SUP-013 asks the service tool to read the last faults, and CON-SUP-113 calls for the last eight fault reports. The item limits history to reports already transmitted. A detected fault can therefore be absent from history if a reset interrupts its serial transmission.
findings.requested_change: Define when a fault report enters history and resolve whether an interrupted transmission affects its availability to GET FAULTS. Record an open point if a product decision is needed.

findings.description: The CON-SUP-113 response template leaves the legal state values and the meaning of fault count undefined. The request boundary is also undefined. A verifier cannot form a complete request or determine the expected response for a known state and fault history.
findings.requested_change: Specify the approved request framing, state encoding and fault-count semantics.

findings.description: The 50 ms deadline in CON-SUP-113 does not identify when receipt is complete or whether the first or final response byte ends the measurement. OP-SYS-007 records these timing references as undecided.
findings.requested_change: Define the observable start and end events for measuring the GET STATUS response time.

findings.description: The item calls for returning the reports in history. CON-SUP-113 does not define their wire order or framing, or how to distinguish a complete response with fewer than eight records, including an empty history.
findings.requested_change: Specify the approved record order, response framing and termination for zero through eight records.

findings.description: The 50 ms response limit from CON-SUP-113 does not say whether timing ends at the first byte or at completion of all returned records. The request-side timing event is also unspecified.
findings.requested_change: Define the observable start and end events for measuring the GET FAULTS response time.

findings.description: The request trigger has no operating-state qualification. A GET FAULTS request received just before a CON-SUP-110 reset may have its response interrupted, and the item also gives no outcome for requests received while the safe state is latched.
findings.requested_change: Specify whether requests are accepted while reset is pending and while the safe state is latched, and define the required outcome for an accepted request overtaken by reset.

findings.description: CON-SUP-113 specifies ERR for other requests, but the item gives neither an approved boundary for recognizing an unrecognized request nor a response deadline. The stated test cannot distinguish a missing ERR from a delayed one.
findings.requested_change: Specify the framing for unrecognized requests and the approved time bound for completing the ERR response.

findings.description: CON-SUP-114 ties the processor-use measurement to the configured core clock. OP-SYS-012 records that the clock setting is absent, and the item does not reference a controlled simulator configuration from which to obtain it. Different settings can yield different results.
findings.requested_change: Reference the approved simulator core-clock setting or controlled profile used to reproduce the processor-use test.

findings.description: The item assigns execution of integration and system tests to the controller software. STK-SUP-015 and CON-SUP-116 require the controller to be testable in Renode and identify the environment for running those tests. They do not assign a test-runner function to the controller.
findings.requested_change: State the simulator compatibility required of the controller and place test execution in the verification environment.

findings.description: The unknown-task test depends on an approved set of supported task identifiers. CON-SUP-115 requires rejection of an unknown task, and CON-SUP-101 names the configured tasks, but neither identifies the complete supported set. The expected result for an identifier outside the default configuration is undefined.
findings.requested_change: Reference the approved supported-task set and use it to select accepted and rejected identifiers for verification.

findings.description: Requiring the history to hold the eight most recent reports leaves older reports in scope for retention and leaves the expected history size undefined before eight faults occur. SYS-DIAG-008 returns the history contents, while CON-SUP-113 limits the service response to the last eight reports.
findings.requested_change: Specify which reports belong to the history exposed to the service tool when fewer than eight faults have occurred and when a new report displaces an older one.

findings.description: The item defines membership by detection, while SYS-DIAG-010 allows entry to occur later, before transmission starts. CON-SUP-110 requires history to survive software and watchdog resets. If a reset occurs after detection and before entry, the expected history contents are undefined.
findings.requested_change: Define when a detected fault becomes part of the retained history and whether a reset before entry changes the reports returned.

findings.description: The test must determine whether the start-up code integrity check correctly accepts or rejects the application image. STK-SUP-007 and CON-SUP-107 identify the image and when to check it, but provide no approved integrity criterion or reference for the expected verdict.
findings.requested_change: Reference the approved image integrity criterion and reference information so tests can establish the expected outcome independently.

findings.description: CON-SUP-107 and the item identify the CRC-32 polynomial. The initialization, reflection and final XOR remain undefined. Different CRC values for the same configuration block can therefore satisfy the stated polynomial constraint, leaving the test without a unique expected value.
findings.requested_change: Reference the complete approved CRC-32 parameters for producing configuration blocks and verifying their stored CRC.

findings.description: Task release requires SYS-CFG-008 to have passed. SYS-CFG-008 defines positive fault-detection conditions only. With a valid block, the absence of a range fault does not establish that the range check has finished, so the release condition can be interpreted differently under CON-SUP-107 and CON-SUP-115.
findings.requested_change: Define a successful range-check outcome that establishes completion before the controller releases an application task.

findings.description: The 11 s limit applies to the duration of each pass but leaves the wait before the first pass and the gaps between passes unbounded. This permits long unchecked intervals even though CON-SUP-108 specifies processing a segment every control cycle and STK-SUP-008 requires repeated background checking.
findings.requested_change: Define when the first run-time pass starts and how successive passes continue, with a controlled reference to the CON-SUP-108 cadence.

findings.description: An 11 s scan can be timed, but the test cannot establish that it completed an integrity check. STK-SUP-008 requires the program-code check to be repeated. The approved image integrity criterion and reference needed to establish the expected result of a run-time pass remain open.
findings.requested_change: Identify the approved integrity criterion and reference for a full run-time pass, and verify its verdict as well as its duration.

findings.description: The required software reset request can be preempted by the window watchdog. For a flow fault at the end of a nominal 10 ms cycle, suppressing that cycle's refresh can leave about 2 ms before the CON-SUP-106 timeout. CON-SUP-110 requires the report and software reset sequence, but gives no precedence rule for this case.
findings.requested_change: Record the approved precedence and define the required reset outcome and deadline when watchdog expiry competes with the supervisor reset request.

findings.description: The instant at which all three signals are low is ambiguous if those signals were already low. For a start-up integrity fault, CON-SUP-109 holds them low from reset. The rationale uses the failing computation's completion as safe-state entry, but the statement does not identify that event as the reference for CON-SUP-110 ordering.
findings.requested_change: Tie the transmission start to safe-state entry for the particular fault and reference the start-up entry event defined by SYS-RST-012.

findings.description: The item adds an exclusive restriction, 'and from no other evidence.' CON-SUP-111 requires classification from the hardware flags but gives no basis for excluding corroborating evidence if the flags are insufficient to distinguish a supervisor reset from another reset.
findings.requested_change: Remove the exclusivity restriction or document its approved basis and show how flag-only classification supports all five classes.

findings.description: The proposed test sets reset-flag patterns and checks the resulting class. CON-SUP-111 names the classes but supplies no mapping or precedence for simultaneous or retained flags. The verifier cannot determine the expected class for those patterns.
findings.requested_change: Reference the approved flag-to-class mapping and define how to handle simultaneous and retained flags in the classification test.

findings.description: This item requires a software reset request following a failed start-up computation. If a watchdog is active during the check, the time remaining after computation may be insufficient for the CON-SUP-110 report and reset sequence. The inputs give neither the start-up watchdog policy nor a bound on the check duration relative to expiry.
findings.requested_change: Resolve watchdog operation during start-up and establish the available time for the report and software reset request after a failing computation.

findings.description: The item requires transmission through the terminating line feed before the software reset request. A CON-SUP-106 window-watchdog reset can interrupt the report first once task-fault refreshes stop. CON-SUP-110 and CON-SUP-112 leave the required report outcome in that case unresolved.
findings.requested_change: State the approved transmission outcome when hardware reset can preempt the report, including whether the full line must be sent and by what deadline.

findings.description: The hold applies 'while the controller is in the safe state,' which the SAFE-001 rationale defines by the output and status levels. A control output going high could itself make that condition false. The obligation needs a hold interval independent of the levels to verify the continued safe state required by STK-SUP-010.
findings.requested_change: Reference safe-state entry and permitted exit events that are independent of the output levels, including the exit condition for a latched safe state.

findings.description: The stated test must observe both outputs low from any reset. CON-SUP-005 identifies the simulator and CON-SUP-003 identifies GPIO, but neither establishes that the test can represent the board-level output during reset assertion and before software configures the pins.
findings.requested_change: Provide verification evidence for both output levels across the whole reset interval for each applicable reset path, and select a method that covers intervals outside the simulator's demonstrated capability.

findings.description: The stated test must observe the external status signal low from any reset, including a reset taken while it is high under SYS-SAFE-006. CON-SUP-003 and CON-SUP-005 provide no evidence that the test represents the status pin level before software can act.
findings.requested_change: Provide verification evidence for the external status level from reset assertion through software takeover for each applicable reset path.

findings.description: The fault-injection test calls for sampling both outputs from the preceding reset. A trace starting once the test build runs cannot establish the uninterrupted hold required by this item and CON-SUP-109 during reset assertion and early start-up.
findings.requested_change: Combine the start-up fault tests with evidence that covers both control output levels from reset assertion to the earliest observation supported by the tests.

findings.description: The proposed test samples the status signal from the preceding reset, but the reset-interval pin behavior is unresolved. An observation made after fault injection can show the low status required at detection and still miss an earlier high level prohibited by CON-SUP-109.
findings.requested_change: Verify the reset and pre-software interval as part of the uninterrupted status hold, alongside the start-up fault tests.

findings.description: The status signal's low level is part of the stated definition of safe state. Tying the hold only to that definition leaves the obligation unclear as soon as the signal goes high. The proposed test also stops at the next reset, although CON-SUP-110 permits only a power-on reset to clear a latched safe state.
findings.requested_change: Define the hold by independent entry and exit events and verify the latched status hold across software and watchdog resets.

findings.description: The item excludes a task period whose control cycle began before the checks passed. Its rationale assumes such a period cannot contain a scheduled release after the checks pass. CON-SUP-102 starts supervision when the checks pass, and CON-SUP-101 does not establish that alignment or the first T_DIAG release phase.
findings.requested_change: Use the approved start-up-to-schedule alignment to define the first counted window and the latest detection point for each task that never completes.

findings.description: The 100 µs deadline for detecting a late start is derived solely from the measurement resolution in CON-SUP-103. That resolution gives no bound on when the controller evaluates the comparison or declares the fault. CON-SUP-105 sets the origin of the safe-state budget.
findings.requested_change: Use a source-supported detection deadline or record the deadline as unresolved. State measurement resolution independently of detection latency.

findings.description: The proposed test infers a 100 µs detection deadline from the fault report. CON-SUP-112 and SYS-DIAG-005 specify a timestamp in milliseconds without approved sub-millisecond precision, and the report does not independently establish when the controller declared the fault.
findings.requested_change: Verify the approved deadline by observing the release, limit expiry and fault declaration on a time base with adequate precision.

findings.description: CON-SUP-103 says an overrun is detected when the execution limit expires. The item waits for the measured value to exceed that limit and permits a further 100 µs. The stated derivation from measurement resolution does not authorize that delay.
findings.requested_change: Reconcile detection at expiry with the permitted completion exactly at the limit, and obtain approval for any allowed detection latency.

findings.description: The proposed test uses execution start plus the limit as a wall-clock expiry even though OP-SYS-013 leaves CPU time versus elapsed time unresolved. It then uses the CON-SUP-112 millisecond timestamp to judge a 100 µs deadline without a defined sub-millisecond format.
findings.requested_change: Use the approved execution-time measure to establish expiry and observe the actual overrun declaration with sufficient time resolution.

findings.description: The item combines the resolution of release-to-start measurement and the resolution of execution-time measurement. Either measurement can meet the CON-SUP-103 resolution while the other fails it, and the rationale already calls for separate exercises.
findings.requested_change: Make the resolution obligations for start delay and execution time independently traceable and judgeable.

findings.description: Testing only at the configured limit and 100 µs above it verifies two fault decisions. Both can be correct with a finer measurement resolution, although the item requires the exact 100 µs resolution specified by CON-SUP-103.
findings.requested_change: Verify the measured increments directly or use observations that distinguish the required granularity from finer and coarser measurements.

findings.description: The statement timestamps arrival when the task signals its checkpoint, while the rationale timestamps receipt by the supervisor. If a signal is issued before the cycle ends and received afterward, the two readings give different fault decisions under CON-SUP-104.
findings.requested_change: Define which event counts as arrival and how the end-of-cycle check treats a checkpoint at the boundary.

findings.description: CON-SUP-104 requires checking the checkpoints of tasks released in that cycle, but the per-task event that produces a checkpoint and the expected number per release remain undefined. T_DIAG can execute for 20 ms under CON-SUP-103, so a completion checkpoint could arrive after its 10 ms release cycle despite compliant execution.
findings.requested_change: Specify the checkpoint event and count per release and define how to judge checkpoints that may arrive after their release cycle.

findings.description: The no-fault decision uses measured delay, but CON-SUP-103 and SYS-SUP-004 give only the 100 µs resolution. A start just after the configured limit can compare equal to the limit or greater than it, depending on how timestamps and configured values are represented.
findings.requested_change: Define or reference the time representation and comparison rule at the start limit, including how to handle times between measurement steps.

findings.description: For a preempted task, its own processor time can be within the CON-SUP-103 limit while elapsed time since execution began exceeds it. The item gives opposite expected fault outcomes depending on which quantity is measured.
findings.requested_change: Specify the execution-time measure and use it for the no-overrun boundary tests, including a preempted execution.

findings.description: The demonstration has no observable success criterion for 'run on the Renode simulator.' Loading the image, booting through the start-up checks and executing supervised cycles are different outcomes. STK-SUP-015 and CON-SUP-116 require a usable environment for simulator-based verification.
findings.requested_change: Define the observable start-up and operational behavior that demonstrates the controller is running on the designated simulator platform.

findings.description: Refresh eligibility is fixed at the cycle boundary, but the refresh follows the flow check. An alive or timing fault detected after the boundary and before the refresh would leave this item requiring the refresh while SYS-WDG-005 forbids it. STK-SUP-005 permits servicing only while the tasks are healthy.
findings.requested_change: Make refresh eligibility cover the instant of actual refresh, while retaining the requirement to include the same cycle's flow check.

findings.description: The timeout is measured from a previous refresh. That gives no expiry reference if the watchdog becomes active and the first refresh never occurs. This case matters to the fallback reset required by STK-SUP-005.
findings.requested_change: Define when the window watchdog becomes active and what event starts the first expiry interval, or reference an approved start-up watchdog rule.

findings.description: The proposed test resets during transmission and then reads GET FAULTS. A report could enter the history after transmission starts but before the injected reset and still pass. That observation can verify survival of an interrupted CON-SUP-112 report, but cannot verify the item's required ordering.
findings.requested_change: Use a test that observes or brackets retained history entry and the first transmitted bit closely enough to detect entry after transmission starts.

findings.description: History membership begins at fault detection in this item. SYS-DIAG-010 permits entry later, before transmission starts. The two rules give different expected histories if GET FAULTS is processed, or if a watchdog reset occurs, between detection and entry. CON-SUP-110 and CON-SUP-113 leave this interval unresolved.
findings.requested_change: Define when a detected fault becomes a history member and what GET FAULTS must return during the interval before entry and after a reset in that interval.

findings.description: Resetting at the first transmitted bit and recovering the report shows that the report was retained at the reset. A history commit coincident with the first bit could also pass that test, although the requirement demands entry strictly before the bit. CON-SUP-110 and CON-SUP-113 provide no ordering at that boundary.
findings.requested_change: If strict precedence is retained, observe the completed history entry and the first transmitted bit as separately ordered events. Make a coincident entry fail.

findings.description: The valid-start test checks that tasks are released after reset. It could pass if a task is released before one of the three checks finishes on a valid image and block. The fault cases check that release is inhibited for selected invalid inputs. CON-SUP-107 requires the integrity checks to precede any release.
findings.requested_change: In the valid-start test, observe completion of all three checks and compare those events with the first release of any application task.

findings.description: The proposed test reads the detection time of a fault injected in the last segment. The fault report gives no completion time for the preceding successful pass, which is the origin of the recurring 11 s bound. Detection in a failing segment also leaves completion of a full successful pass unobserved.
findings.requested_change: Observe successful full-pass completion events on a common time base. Measure the first interval from the first eligible cycle start and each subsequent interval from the preceding pass completion.

findings.description: The transmission is ordered against the first all-low instant strictly after detection. If a second fault is detected while all three signals are already low, or if they become low at the detection instant, that wording fails to identify a distinct entry event. CON-SUP-110 requires the entry event to establish transmission order.
findings.requested_change: Define the timing reference when the signals are already low or become low coincident with detection. Use the same entry rule for the reset deadline in SYS-RST-001.

findings.description: The ordering applies only if the fault results in a software reset request. Under CON-SUP-106 and STK-SUP-005, the window watchdog can reset the controller first, before the report required by CON-SUP-110 and CON-SUP-112. In that case the ordering obligation never applies and the report can be lost.
findings.requested_change: Resolve watchdog precedence and specify the report and reset behaviour for the resulting sequence, including any case in which a hardware reset interrupts it.

findings.description: The test says to set reset-flag patterns and check that the class follows the flags. CON-SUP-111 names the five classes but supplies no expected mapping for combined flags or flags retained from an earlier reset. Those cases have no expected test result.
findings.requested_change: Reference an approved mapping and precedence rule, then give expected classes for individual, combined and retained flag patterns.

findings.description: The test takes the start of the hold interval from the millisecond fault timestamp in SYS-DIAG-005. A low-to-high transition near a CON-SUP-105 fault event can fall within that timestamp's uncertainty. Starting each test with both outputs high also leaves the case of an output already low at detection untested.
findings.requested_change: Observe the rule-defined fault event and both output transitions on a common time base. Include cases with either output already low at that event.

findings.description: The test uses the millisecond timestamp in SYS-DIAG-005 to start the hold observation. It cannot resolve the order of a nearby low-to-high status transition and the CON-SUP-105 fault event. Testing only from an initially high status also leaves the already-low case untested.
findings.requested_change: Observe the rule-defined fault event and status transitions on a common time base. Exercise the hold with the status signal already low as well as initially high.

findings.description: If a task begins at the first instant its measured delay exceeds the limit, it has begun by that instant, so this trigger can be false. SYS-SUP-006 also leaves that case outside its scope because the measured delay exceeds the limit. CON-SUP-103 classifies a start later than the limit as a late start.
findings.requested_change: Cover a task that starts with a measured delay above the limit, including a start coincident with the first above-limit measurement. Define how to avoid a second declaration if the pending release was already declared late.

findings.description: The delayed-start test can pass if the controller waits for the task to begin before declaring the fault. The test checks that the first report bit follows limit expiry and acknowledges that this bit does not establish when the declaration occurred.
findings.requested_change: Observe fault declaration directly in the delayed-start test and compare it with the applicable trigger and actual task start. Exercise the pending-release case separately.

findings.description: The statement requires declaration at the exact instant the execution limit expires. The rationale says that exact declaration is infeasible and proposes testing against a tolerance that has yet to be approved. CON-SUP-103 supplies the expiry event and a measurement resolution.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the permitted declaration latency from expiry and align the normative wording and verification tolerance with that decision.

findings.description: This item declares an overrun at expiry if the task is still executing. SYS-SUP-007 forbids an overrun for a completion measured at or below the limit. A completion just after expiry can satisfy both conditions if the 100 µs measurement maps it to the limit, as OP-SYS-027 describes.
findings.requested_change: Use a consistent basis for the expiry and no-overrun decisions. Define and verify the outcomes at expiry and for completions that measure equal to the limit just after expiry.

findings.description: The test requires a monotonic mapping and strictly less than 100 µs error against injected delays. CON-SUP-103 specifies measurement resolution. OP-SYS-027 leaves the mapping and alignment undecided, so the proposed pass criteria can reject a measurement based on properties beyond the stated resolution.
findings.requested_change: Verify the measurement increments required by this item. Apply error and input-to-output mapping criteria once they have an approved basis.

findings.description: The item treats a checkpoint received exactly at the cycle end as missing. CON-SUP-104 and CON-SUP-105 place the check at that boundary but do not establish precedence between receipt and evaluation when they coincide. The chosen precedence changes whether a program-flow fault is declared.
findings.requested_change: Obtain an approved rule for coincident receipt and evaluation, record it in the requirement, and test the exact boundary.

findings.description: The late-checkpoint test expects to verify the following cycle's decision. SYS-WDG-003 withholds the refresh on the faulty cycle, and SYS-WDG-006 can reset the controller before that next decision. An absence of a second code 4 report could therefore pass without demonstrating that the late checkpoint was discarded.
findings.requested_change: Demonstrate that a later flow evaluation actually occurred and excluded the late checkpoint, or use analysis to verify exclusion where the normal reset sequence prevents that observation.

findings.description: The item prohibits a late-start fault when the measured delay equals the limit. With a 2 ms limit and truncation, a start at 2.05 ms could be measured at 2.0 ms and be accepted, although CON-SUP-103 classifies a start later than the limit as late. OP-SYS-027 leaves that mapping unresolved.
findings.requested_change: Resolve how actual start times map to the measured boundary, then confirm the comparison against CON-SUP-103 and verify a start just beyond the limit.

findings.description: The demonstration checks for the presence of the SYS-RST-009 message. With the message identity unresolved under CON-SUP-111, the procedure cannot distinguish that message from a startup FLT line or other simulated serial output.
findings.requested_change: Define how the demonstration identifies the startup message and use that criterion to check the simulated serial output.

findings.description: The rationale says refresh is forbidden as soon as a fault becomes detectable under CON-SUP-105. The statement only ends the obligation to refresh at that instant. SYS-WDG-005 prohibits refresh after detection, which SYS-SUP-002 and SYS-SUP-003 distinguish from detectability. This leaves refresh eligibility unresolved between those events.
findings.requested_change: Define one refresh cutoff for STK-SUP-005 and use it consistently for both the eligibility rule and the prohibition on further refreshes.

findings.description: The verification asks for an alive fault whose detectability instant falls strictly after the cycle boundary and before its refresh. SYS-SUP-001 ties an alive-window end to a control-cycle boundary. Injecting an off-boundary alive event would bypass the rule this test is meant to exercise.
findings.requested_change: Exercise alive fault eligibility at the coincident cycle boundary. Use a timing fault with a valid detectability instant to test the interval between that boundary and refresh.

findings.description: When faults with the same detection instant straddle the eighth-report cutoff, either report could be displaced under '8 most recently detected faults'. CON-SUP-113 gives the count but does not resolve that tie, which changes the result returned by GET FAULTS.
findings.requested_change: Define how simultaneous faults are selected at the eight-report cutoff and verify which report is retained.

findings.description: At the eighth detection or any later detection, this item immediately changes the required history membership. SYS-DIAG-010 permits entry later, before the first transmitted bit. A query or reset in that gap leaves the required report and the displaced report unresolved under CON-SUP-110 and CON-SUP-113.
findings.requested_change: Define one event that changes the eight-report history and specify the observable contents before that event and after an intervening reset.

findings.description: A fault reported in the expected cycle for one selected segment does not establish the CON-SUP-108 cadence. An implementation could process additional segments elsewhere, or handle the final partial segment or the next-pass restart incorrectly, and still pass that observation.
findings.requested_change: Observe the image range and processing count per cycle across a pass boundary. Include an image with a partial final segment and verify that the next pass restarts at __app_start in the following cycle.

findings.description: The ordering applies only if the failing startup check leads to a software reset request. If a watchdog is already active during startup, it can reset the controller after the failing computation and before the report or software reset request. CON-SUP-106 and CON-SUP-107 provide no startup watchdog behaviour or timing evidence that rules out this sequence.
findings.requested_change: Resolve watchdog behaviour during startup and specify how the required report sequence is preserved or handled if a watchdog reset can intervene.

findings.description: The continuous low-output obligation includes reset assertion and the interval before software can act. CON-SUP-003 identifies available GPIOs but gives no pin-level or board evidence for those intervals. The proposed simulator sampling does not establish that both outputs remain driven low across each reset.
findings.requested_change: Establish how both outputs are held low through the specified reset paths and use verification evidence that covers the full reset and startup intervals.

findings.description: The status signal must remain low continuously across each reset while the safe state is latched. CON-SUP-003 gives no status-pin behaviour during reset or before software configures it. The proposed simulator check for no high sample cannot establish that the signal stayed low during those intervals.
findings.requested_change: Establish how the status signal is held low through the specified reset paths and verify that the signal remains low throughout each reset and startup interval.

findings.description: The text covers the execution time of every release. The verification asks for a value at completion for overrunning releases, then allows testing a controller that stops measuring at limit expiry. CON-SUP-103 requires timing supervision at expiry, but the item leaves the required measurement endpoint unclear for overruns and releases that never start.
findings.requested_change: Define which started or unstarted releases require an execution-time measurement, when that measurement ends, and whether a value at overrun completion is required. Align the test with that scope.

findings.description: The test requires measured values to be monotonic and to differ from injected execution times by strictly less than 100 µs. CON-SUP-103 supplies a resolution and OP-SYS-027 leaves the mapping and alignment open. The proposed test can reject an implementation based on measurement properties outside the stated requirement.
findings.requested_change: Verify the required measurement increments. Apply accuracy and mapping criteria once they have an approved basis.

findings.description: The indication is cited as evidence of successful startup checks, but observing a high simulated status signal alone could pass if the controller drives it high before the checks finish. CON-SUP-109 requires the signal to be low until those checks pass.
findings.requested_change: Tie the observed high transition to successful completion of the startup checks. Make an early assertion fail the demonstration.

findings.description: The item prescribes 11 s of uninterrupted high status after SYS-TEST-004. CON-SUP-108 supplies 11 s for a code-check pass, measured from a different event. STK-SUP-015 and CON-SUP-116 require simulator verification but supply no 11 s acceptance interval for the status signal.
findings.requested_change: Use an approved demonstration duration and start event tied to the supervised operation the demonstration is intended to exercise.

findings.description: The rationale treats an uninterrupted high status signal as proof that all four tasks, control cycles and watchdog refreshes ran. A controller that sets status high and then stalls with the simulated watchdogs inactive would pass the high-status observation.
findings.requested_change: Observe positive evidence of task execution, control-cycle progression and watchdog refreshes during the same interval used to demonstrate sustained high status.

findings.description: The item prescribes 11 s without a fault report. CON-SUP-112 specifies how to report a detected fault, and CON-SUP-108 gives a run-time code-check pass bound. Neither establishes the proposed observation interval for this simulator demonstration.
findings.requested_change: Reference an approved duration and start event for observing fault reporting during fault-free supervised operation.

findings.description: The rationale treats the absence of a fault report line as evidence that no faults were detected during supervised operation. A stalled supervisor, an unobserved serial path, or a reset that truncates a CON-SUP-112 fault report could all produce the same observation.
findings.requested_change: Establish that supervision runs and the simulated serial path is observable during the interval. Define how the demonstration detects fault declarations and handles partial reports or resets.

findings.description: The first transmitted bit supplies the only deadline for completing the history entry. If a watchdog reset prevents transmission from starting, the item gives no expected history outcome. CON-SUP-110 requires retention across watchdog resets, and OP-SYS-015 records the unresolved treatment of a fault detected before such a reset.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the expected history contents when reset interrupts the sequence before the first bit, and specify a verification case for that outcome.

findings.description: The proposed first-bit reset test reads GET FAULTS after restart. That answer can contain the report even if startup reconstructed it from separately retained fault data and the history entry was incomplete at the first bit. This test observes the retention outcome of CON-SUP-110 without establishing the ordering this item requires.
findings.requested_change: Observe completion of the retained history entry and transmission of the first bit on a common time base. Use the post-reset read as separate evidence of retention.

findings.description: The valid-start check treats absence of a first task release as failure of this item, although the item and CON-SUP-107 impose a release gate. It gives no deadline by which a release must occur. A run with no release cannot demonstrate the event ordering.
findings.requested_change: Require an observed release for a valid ordering demonstration and classify a missing release under a separately sourced startup progression criterion or as an invalid ordering run.

findings.description: The proposed timing test defines completion as processing the segment ending at __app_end without a fault. A check that skips an earlier segment and processes the last segment on time can meet that criterion without completing the full pass required by CON-SUP-108 and SYS-MEM-007.
findings.requested_change: Count only completion events backed by evidence that the whole image was processed in that pass, and apply the 11 s bounds to those events.

findings.description: The supplementary fault test requires code 7 on the serial line in the cycle that processed the corrupted segment. CON-SUP-105 starts the reaction at completion of the failing computation, OP-SYS-005 leaves the integrity method open, and CON-SUP-112 allows serial reporting within 10 ms of detection. A whole-image check or a report crossing a cycle boundary can satisfy those inputs and fail this criterion.
findings.requested_change: Judge segment cadence from the processed-range trace. Judge injected corruption against the selected integrity method's detection event and the applicable diagnostic timing.

findings.description: CON-SUP-110 orders safe-state entry before fault-report transmission. For a task fault, SYS-WDG-007 can withhold the refresh and CON-SUP-106 can reset the controller before safe-state entry or the start of transmission. The item requires transmission to start and gives no applicable outcome when that reset preempts it.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the precedence of watchdog reset and fault reporting, then state the expected transmission outcome if a watchdog reset preempts safe-state entry or reporting.

findings.description: The text prohibits rises 'between' the CON-SUP-105 event and the next reset. The rationale rejects a rise at the event itself. Those readings give different verdicts when a previously low control output rises at the fault event.
findings.requested_change: State explicitly that the prohibition covers the fault event itself and ends at the next reset.

findings.description: The text prohibits rises 'between' the CON-SUP-105 event and the next reset. The rationale rejects a rise at the event itself. A status transition coinciding with the fault event therefore has different verdicts under the text and the proposed test.
findings.requested_change: State explicitly that the status-signal prohibition covers the fault event itself and ends at the next reset.

findings.description: The verification rationale would apply the future detection deadline from the first measured value above the limit. OP-SYS-025 asks for a deadline from expiry of the configured start limit. CON-SUP-103 quantization can put the measured crossing later, allowing the proposed comparison to accept a declaration beyond a deadline measured from expiry.
findings.requested_change: Use the approved origin for any separate detection deadline. Record the configured limit expiry and the measured threshold crossing as distinct events.

findings.description: The sweep accepts any set of 100 µs multiples containing a pair 100 µs apart. A readout alternating between 0 and 100 µs regardless of the injected start delay passes, although CON-SUP-103 requires measurement of the task's start delay.
findings.requested_change: Verify that the readout tracks the interval from release to first execution and advances in 100 µs increments. Apply the mapping and alignment once approved in OP-SYS-027.

findings.description: CON-SUP-104 and CON-SUP-105 place the flow check and its fault event at the end of the cycle. The item defers the verdict for receipt at that same instant to OP-SYS-036. Either a valid checkpoint or a missing-checkpoint fault is possible under the current text.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the precedence of receipt and evaluation at the cycle boundary and use it to determine the coincident-receipt test verdict.

findings.description: The proposed sweep checks multiples of 100 µs and the presence of one pair 100 µs apart. These criteria can pass values unrelated to execution time or calculated from the wrong start event. They do not establish the interval from execution start to completion or limit expiry required by the item and grounded in CON-SUP-103.
findings.requested_change: Compare the measured values with the specified execution interval in both completion and overrun runs, using the approved execution-time measure and quantization rules.

findings.description: Analysis criterion (d) requires that no prior-cycle order or count state be carried into the evaluation. CON-SUP-104 and the item constrain which checkpoints can affect the result. An evaluation can retain tagged prior-cycle state and filter it out before it affects presence, count or order, yet fail criterion (d).
findings.requested_change: Trace every retained state path and require evidence that prior-cycle state cannot affect the current evaluation.

findings.description: The nominal run observes a low-to-high edge, and SYS-TEST-007 through SYS-TEST-009 observe failure runs. All four can pass if a valid startup drives status high while its full checks are still running and the injected-failure paths suppress that edge. The rationale claims these runs demonstrate the ordering required by CON-SUP-109.
findings.requested_change: In the nominal run, observe each successful startup check's completion and the status edge on a common time base, and compare their order.

findings.description: The proposed requirement mandates an 11 s high-status interval starting at the status edge. CON-SUP-108 gives 11 s for a full run-time integrity pass, with a different timing origin. STK-SUP-015 and CON-SUP-116 supply no high-status demonstration duration, and OP-SYS-029 records that this duration awaits approval.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the demonstration duration and its timing origin, then use the approved interval in this item and its dependent demonstrations.

findings.description: The absence of the four-character FLT prefix does not establish the rationale's claimed absence of fault declarations. A late fault can leave only a partial prefix in the capture and drive status low after the 11 s status observation ends. A later GET STATUS reply and an alive-fault positive control can still pass. Under OP-SYS-007, a report starting within the CON-SUP-112 deadline may finish its prefix after the capture closes.
findings.requested_change: Define frame and capture boundaries that cover the approved report deadline and account for partial transmissions. Use direct declaration evidence if the verdict is intended to establish absence of detected faults.

findings.description: The observation interval ends with a complete code 5 report, but the setup does not establish an otherwise valid startup and gives no verdict when that report never arrives. A configuration fault can keep status low while masking whether the injected code-integrity case was exercised under CON-SUP-107 and CON-SUP-112.
findings.requested_change: Establish an otherwise valid startup, isolate the injected code-integrity failure, and require observation of a complete code 5 report for a pass.

findings.description: The observation interval ends with a complete code 6 report, but the setup does not establish an intact application image and gives no verdict when that report never arrives. A startup code-integrity failure can keep status low without exercising the intended configuration-integrity failure under CON-SUP-107 and CON-SUP-112.
findings.requested_change: Use an intact application image and isolate the configuration-integrity failure. Require observation of a complete code 6 report for a pass.

findings.description: The setup does not establish that the code and configuration integrity checks can pass with the injected range fault. A modification that invalidates the stored CRC can produce code 6 and keep status low without exercising CON-SUP-115. The end of the observation interval is undefined if the code 9 line never arrives.
findings.requested_change: Specify a range-fault stimulus that preserves integrity-check validity, and require observation of a complete code 9 report for a pass.

findings.description: The minimum of 1099 complete cycles assumes that the first cycle starts within 10 ms of the status edge. CON-SUP-101 specifies the cycle period, and CON-SUP-109 defines the status signal. Neither bounds the delay between those events. A controller can meet the sourced cycle period and miss the count.
findings.requested_change: Use an approved first-cycle alignment and observation interval to derive the minimum count, or anchor the count to an observed cycle boundary.

findings.description: Completion is due by the execution-limit expiry of each scheduled release. If a scheduled task never starts, there is no execution-limit expiry to observe under CON-SUP-103 and SYS-SUP-003. The item does not give a finite failure criterion for the missing release or start, despite claiming evidence of execution for every CON-SUP-101 slot.
findings.requested_change: Enumerate expected releases from the configured schedule. Define finite failure criteria for missing releases or starts and check each observed completion against its applicable execution limit.

findings.description: The minimum of 1098 refreshes inherits the unapproved first-cycle delay used for SYS-TEST-010. CON-SUP-106 requires a refresh at the end of each eligible cycle and defines inter-refresh timing. It does not give a refresh count measured from the status edge.
findings.requested_change: Derive the threshold from an approved observation interval and cycle alignment, or evaluate refreshes against the observed eligible cycle ends.

findings.description: The count and 6–12 ms spacing can pass when refreshes are shifted away from cycle ends, or when one cycle is skipped and another has two refreshes. These criteria do not verify the once-per-cycle, end-of-cycle service described in the rationale and required by CON-SUP-106.
findings.requested_change: Associate each observed refresh with its eligible control cycle and verify both the cycle-end service and the inter-refresh window.

findings.description: The phrase 'contains no refresh' leaves interval endpoints undefined. With inclusive endpoints, refreshes exactly 100 ms apart can satisfy the wording even though SYS-WDG-004 requires intervals shorter than the 100 ms timeout in CON-SUP-106.
findings.requested_change: Define the leading and trailing observation boundaries and state explicitly how a gap of exactly 100 ms is judged.

findings.description: The item mandates a line feed for the GET STATUS reply. CON-SUP-113 specifies the STS fields and response limit without specifying that terminator. CON-SUP-112 specifies a line feed for FLT reports. The proposed criterion also accepts a bare STS prefix followed by a line feed, without the required fields.
findings.requested_change: Verify that the response contains both fields required by CON-SUP-113. Source its framing or record the framing as an open point before imposing a terminator.

findings.description: The item measures the 50 ms limit from the end of the request, and 'transmit' leaves the response endpoint open. CON-SUP-113 gives the duration, and OP-SYS-007 records that its measurement endpoints remain undecided. A reply starting before the deadline and finishing after it has no unique verdict.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the request and response timing endpoints and make both explicit in the demonstration criterion.

findings.description: The 40 ms derivation assumes T_IN's 10 ms periods are already progressing at injection. The 100 ms offset from the status edge supplies no such guarantee under CON-SUP-101 or CON-SUP-102, and OP-SYS-020 leaves first-cycle alignment open. Injection before the first period can fail the test on a controller that satisfies the alive rule.
findings.requested_change: Specify a separate positive-control run on the nominal build and configuration. Qualify the injection instant against observed T_IN period boundaries and derive the report deadline from the resulting alive-window expiry and approved transmission endpoint.

findings.description: The cutoff for late start is physical limit expiry, while SYS-SUP-002 classifies lateness at the first measured value above the limit. If quantization separates those events, a refresh can fall between them. A task starting just after that refresh can still be judged on time, while an otherwise identical run can later be judged late. The obligation depends on a future start decision.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the late-start threshold mapping and define a refresh cutoff that can be determined from information available at the refresh. Align that cutoff with SYS-WDG-007.

findings.description: Fault-free run V1 accepts a refresh anywhere between successive cycle boundaries after the flow check. That permits alternating early and late refreshes whose spacing falls outside the 6–12 ms window in CON-SUP-106. It also leaves the meaning of service at the end of the cycle unverified.
findings.requested_change: Verify the association and allowed delay between the cycle end, flow-check completion and refresh, and check the observed inter-refresh intervals against CON-SUP-106.

findings.description: The inclusive refresh prohibition can produce a window-watchdog reset 12 ms after the previous refresh under CON-SUP-106. That reset can interrupt CON-SUP-110's report-then-software-reset sequence, and a watchdog reset does not satisfy its consecutive supervisor-reset latch rule.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the precedence of watchdog reset, report transmission and supervisor reset, including the effect of a preempting watchdog reset on the latch sequence.

findings.description: The item prohibits a refresh at the exact cutoff. The V3 cases inherited from SYS-WDG-003 put expiry strictly before or strictly after the reference refresh, and the extra overrun run does not require coincidence. A strict-after implementation can pass these cases while permitting a coincident refresh.
findings.requested_change: Add a valid case or analysis that distinguishes a refresh coinciding with the cutoff from one immediately before it.

findings.description: CON-SUP-101 requires T_IN, T_CTRL and T_OUT to be released in that order each 10 ms cycle. SYS-CFG-002 gives their configured periods and SYS-CFG-004 gives checkpoint order. An implementation can release the three tasks in a different order and still produce checkpoints in the configured order.
findings.requested_change: Capture the required default release sequence separately from checkpoint order and trace it to CON-SUP-101.

findings.description: SYS-RST-012 requires a software reset for configuration-integrity failure while SYS-RST-003 latches the safe state for a range fault. SYS-MEM-002 and SYS-CFG-008 leave open whether a corrupted block can be range-checked and latch the safe state before its failed CRC comparison is known. CON-SUP-107 and CON-SUP-115 do not settle which outcome applies when both checks fail.
findings.requested_change: Record and resolve the validity and precedence rules for startup checks when an integrity failure and a range violation can both be observed. Apply the agreed diagnostic and recovery outcomes to that case.

findings.description: After a repeated-fault latch and a subsequent startup that passes all checks, SYS-SAFE-010 and SYS-SAFE-011 hold the external signals low. The set leaves it open whether application releases, alive supervision and runtime integrity checking proceed in that state. SYS-MEM-004, SYS-SUP-001 and SYS-MEM-008 use startup-check completion without a common mode rule for retained-latch startup.
findings.requested_change: Disposition which application and supervisor functions are active when startup checks pass with the safe state still latched, and align their entry conditions with the agreed behavior under CON-SUP-110.

findings.description: The startup message, asynchronous fault reports and service replies use the same CON-SUP-007 serial line. SYS-RST-009, SYS-DIAG-002 and SYS-DIAG-007 through SYS-DIAG-009 do not say how an in-progress response or multiple pending reports are handled when a fault report becomes due. OP-SYS-033 covers a later fault near software reset, leaving transmission already in progress and simultaneous demand open.
findings.requested_change: Identify the permitted concurrent traffic and frame-handling rules. Check the admitted report and reply lengths and scheduling against the 115200 baud line and the applicable deadlines.

findings.description: CON-SUP-107 gives a configuration block with a stored CRC, and SYS-CFG-001 and SYS-MEM-002 depend on the same block. OP-SYS-005 records CRC algorithm parameters but leaves the byte range and treatment of the stored CRC field unspecified. A producer and checker can use the same CRC parameters and disagree on the result.
findings.requested_change: Record the configuration producer/checker interface decision for the covered bytes, their serialization and the treatment of the stored CRC field. Use it to define reproducible valid and invalid blocks.

findings.description: Several rationales direct readers to the wrong requirement after the fault-reaction items were split. SYS-SAFE-007 and SYS-SAFE-008 point to SYS-SAFE-003 for the latched hold, which is now in SYS-SAFE-010 and SYS-SAFE-011. SYS-RST-012 points to SYS-RST-002 for report-before-reset ordering, which is stated in SYS-RST-013.
findings.requested_change: Update the rationales and open-point references to identify the current requirements that own each hold, transition and ordering rule.

findings.description: STK-SUP-005 limits service of both watchdogs to healthy tasks. SYS-WDG-003 and SYS-WDG-007 treat a detectable task fault as the end of health for window-watchdog service. SYS-WDG-004 and SYS-WDG-005 still use declaration for independent-watchdog service, so a pending declaration can leave an independent refresh required after the set already treats the task as unhealthy.
findings.requested_change: Define the health transition that governs each watchdog. Use the same transition unless an approved distinction explains how both service rules satisfy STK-SUP-005.

findings.description: SYS-RST-002 defines an entry instant per fault, including when all three signals are already low at detection. SYS-RST-001 starts the CON-SUP-110 reset deadline from an instant when the signals are low, which can describe a whole interval. OP-SYS-033 acknowledges the missing alignment in addition to the separate decision about a later fault.
findings.requested_change: Use the defined safe-state entry event for the first fault's reset deadline and keep any change to that deadline for a later fault subject to the precedence decision in OP-SYS-033.

findings.description: SYS-WDG-006 expires the window after 12 ms without a further refresh. CON-SUP-106 makes a refresh later than 12 ms invalid, and SYS-TEST-012 accepts spacing of exactly 12 ms. The set gives no ordering for a refresh coincident with expiry, so the watchdog and demonstration can yield different outcomes at that boundary.
findings.requested_change: Define the refresh-versus-expiry ordering at exactly 12 ms consistently with CON-SUP-106, and use it in the watchdog and demonstration verdicts.

findings.description: The trace matrix gives derivation links for SYS-TEST-005 from CON-SUP-108 and for SYS-TEST-010 and SYS-TEST-012 from the cycle and watchdog constraints. These items are marked derived=false even though their rationales say the timing origin or counts rely on unapproved assumptions. The links identify the related inputs but misstate the basis for the normative test targets.
findings.requested_change: Identify direct obligations and proposed derivations accurately in the items and trace. Trace the demonstration targets to approved premises or retain them as open proposals pending a decision.

findings.description: A refresh follows the completed flow check under SYS-WDG-003. With 10 ms cycle boundaries and variable delays from those boundaries to refresh, the inter-refresh interval is 10 ms plus the change in delay between cycles. CON-SUP-106 limits that interval to 6–12 ms. OP-SYS-013 identifies execution loads, but the set gives no bound or feasibility criterion for that variation.
findings.requested_change: Assess the variation in cycle-end-to-refresh delay under the configured schedule, including flow checking and interference, and link its allowable range to the window-watchdog limits.

findings.description: SYS-RST-004 through SYS-RST-007 and SYS-DIAG-010 depend on state that survives software and watchdog resets under CON-SUP-110. The environment analysis leaves open whether the selected target and Renode model preserve the relevant state through those reset paths and whether a reset during an update leaves a usable record. OP-SYS-015 and OP-SYS-022 address required history contents, but do not establish these platform capabilities.
findings.requested_change: Record the platform and simulator dependencies for retaining reset-sequence state, the latch and history, including interrupted updates. Assign an evidence method for each retention property.

findings.description: SYS-BL-1 is marked draft, but several open points that change required outcomes are marked blocks=false. For example, OP-SYS-027 changes which releases satisfy CON-SUP-103, OP-SYS-007 changes the timing verdict under CON-SUP-112 and CON-SUP-113, and OP-SYS-015 changes the reset-surviving history. The disposition understates what needs agreement before those outcomes can be baselined.
findings.requested_change: Reconcile open-point blocking flags and affected-item statuses with the unresolved changes to behavior and verification, and identify the decisions or evidence required to close them.

findings.description: Suppressing T_IN completion can also suppress its checkpoint or force a timing fault, depending on the hook behavior and checkpoint source. Under SYS-SUP-005 and SYS-WDG-007, an earlier flow or timing fault can initiate reset before the two-period alive window expires. SYS-TEST-015 gives no validity criterion that distinguishes a masked alive test from a failure of alive supervision.
findings.requested_change: Show that the stimulus prevents completion without an earlier competing fault, or define another observation that isolates the alive monitor. Treat runs masked by an earlier fault or reset as invalid for the positive control.

findings.description: The refresh interval applies whenever no listed task fault has been detected since reset. This includes startup and a retained safe-state latch, where CON-SUP-106 does not establish when independent-watchdog servicing applies and OP-SYS-010 remains open.
findings.requested_change: Specify the operating states in which the independent watchdog is serviced and the event that anchors its first refresh interval.

findings.description: Stopping both refreshes on a task fault can put the CON-SUP-106 window-watchdog reset ahead of the report and software reset in CON-SUP-110 and CON-SUP-112. The required outcome near window expiry remains unresolved.
findings.requested_change: Align refresh cessation with the approved precedence for hardware expiry, reporting and software reset.

findings.description: The CON-SUP-110 latch rule still leaves the effect of an intervening watchdog or other reset undefined. The rationale describes fault-free operation after successful startup, but the normative text does not identify the event that starts the 60 s interval.
findings.requested_change: State which intervening events break the sequence and identify the approved start event for counting 60 s of fault-free operation.

findings.description: CON-SUP-111 requires a startup message carrying the reset cause. Without the framing and encoding left open in OP-SYS-002, the verifier cannot identify the message and decode a cause.
findings.requested_change: Reference an approved startup-message format and give the expected encoding for each reset class.

findings.description: CON-SUP-111 requires the service tool to read the reset cause. Neither response in CON-SUP-113 includes it and other requests receive ERR. The set leaves the interaction that satisfies both constraints open.
findings.requested_change: Specify the approved service interaction that delivers the cause, and reconcile it with the CON-SUP-113 response rules.

findings.description: The 10 ms requirement leaves it open whether to time the first transmitted bit or completion of the terminating line feed. The rationale selects completion while OP-SYS-007 records that the CON-SUP-112 endpoint is undecided.
findings.requested_change: State the approved observable endpoint for the 10 ms deadline in the requirement and use it in verification.

findings.description: The report is due for every detected fault under CON-SUP-112. SYS-WDG-005 can cause a CON-SUP-106 reset before transmission starts or completes. The report obligation in that case remains undefined.
findings.requested_change: Apply the approved watchdog precedence to define the required report outcome when reset preempts transmission.

findings.description: SYS-DIAG-003 assigns code 8 to a watchdog reset and SYS-DIAG-002 requires an entity. The task names, CODE and CONFIG in CON-SUP-112 leave code 8 without an entity value.
findings.requested_change: Specify the approved entity value for a watchdog-reset report.

findings.description: The affected task is ambiguous when several checkpoints are missing or out of order in one CON-SUP-104 evaluation. The set leaves the entity required by CON-SUP-112 undecided in that case.
