findings.requested_change: Specify the approved task-selection and reporting rule for flow faults involving one or multiple incorrect checkpoints.

findings.description: CON-SUP-112 gives milliseconds since start without defining the reference event. The item selects the latest reset and uses 'the controller started', which identifies no observable event while OP-SYS-007 remains unresolved.
findings.requested_change: Define the approved timestamp origin as an observable event and apply it after each relevant reset class.

findings.description: CON-SUP-113 supplies the STS template, but the request boundary, legal state values and meaning of fault count remain open. A verifier cannot form a complete request and predict the response for a known state and history.
findings.requested_change: Specify the approved request framing, state encoding and fault-count semantics.

findings.description: The 50 ms deadline from CON-SUP-113 leaves request receipt and response transmission without agreed measurement endpoints. A reply that starts within 50 ms and finishes later has no unique verdict.
findings.requested_change: Define the observable request and response events that bound the GET STATUS response time.

findings.description: CON-SUP-113 requires the last eight reports, but the set leaves their wire order and response framing open. A verifier cannot distinguish a complete response holding fewer than eight reports, including an empty response, from an incomplete transmission.
findings.requested_change: Specify the approved record order, framing and completion indication for histories containing zero through eight reports.

findings.description: The 50 ms deadline from CON-SUP-113 has no agreed request-side event or endpoint for a multi-record response. A reply may start within 50 ms and finish after it.
findings.requested_change: Define the observable request and response events that bound the GET FAULTS response time.

findings.description: The GET FAULTS trigger has no mode qualification. A CON-SUP-110 reset can interrupt an accepted response, and the set leaves acceptance and response behavior in the latched safe state open.
findings.requested_change: Define acceptance during pending reset and latched operation, and state the expected outcome when reset overtakes an accepted request.

findings.description: CON-SUP-113 requires ERR for other requests. Without request framing or an approved response bound, a test cannot establish when recognition is due or distinguish a missing ERR from a delayed one.
findings.requested_change: Define how an unrecognized request is delimited and give the approved deadline for observing its ERR response.

findings.description: CON-SUP-114 requires processor-use measurement at the configured core clock. The set gives neither the clock setting nor a controlled simulator configuration that supplies it, so the result is not reproducible.
findings.requested_change: Reference the approved clock setting or controlled simulator configuration for the processor-use test.

findings.description: CON-SUP-115 requires rejection of unknown tasks. CON-SUP-101 gives the configured tasks but leaves the supported identifier set open. The expected verdict for an identifier outside the default configuration is therefore undefined.
findings.requested_change: Reference the approved supported-task set and use it to select known and unknown identifiers for verification.

findings.description: STK-SUP-007 and CON-SUP-107 identify the application image and when to check it. The approved integrity criterion and reference needed for an independent accept-or-reject verdict remain open.
findings.requested_change: Reference the approved integrity criterion and reference information used to establish the expected result for each test image.

findings.description: CON-SUP-107 gives the CRC-32 polynomial. Different initialization, reflection and final XOR settings can produce different check values for the same block while using that polynomial.
findings.requested_change: Reference the complete approved CRC-32 parameters so an independent verifier can compute the expected value.

findings.description: A flow fault at the end of a nominal 10 ms cycle can suppress the refresh with about 2 ms remaining before the CON-SUP-106 timeout. That reset can preempt the CON-SUP-110 software reset request and prevent it from counting toward the latch.
findings.requested_change: Apply the approved reset precedence and state the required reset outcome and timing when hardware expiry competes with the software reset request.

findings.description: The software reset is required after a failed startup computation. With a watchdog active during the check, the remaining time after failure may be insufficient for the CON-SUP-110 report and reset sequence. Startup watchdog operation and the available time remain open.
findings.requested_change: Resolve startup watchdog operation and establish the time available for reporting and requesting reset after a failed computation.

findings.description: The terminating line feed must precede a software reset request. If refreshes stop and CON-SUP-106 resets the controller first, that ordering can hold vacuously while the CON-SUP-110 and CON-SUP-112 report is interrupted.
findings.requested_change: State the required transmission outcome when the hardware reset preempts the intended software reset request.

findings.description: The test must establish both outputs low from any reset under CON-SUP-109. CON-SUP-003 and CON-SUP-005 do not establish that the simulator represents external pin levels during reset assertion and before software configures the pins.
findings.requested_change: Use a verification method that establishes both output levels through reset and software takeover for every applicable reset path.

findings.description: CON-SUP-109 requires status low from any reset, including one taken while SYS-SAFE-006 has status high. The stated test lacks evidence that the external status level is represented while reset is asserted and before software acts.
findings.requested_change: Establish how the external status level will be verified from reset assertion through software takeover for each applicable reset path.

findings.description: The startup fault test samples the two outputs from the preceding reset. A trace beginning once the test build runs cannot establish the continuous low interval required by CON-SUP-109 through reset assertion and early startup.
findings.requested_change: Combine the injected-fault test with verification evidence covering both outputs from reset assertion to the earliest supported test observation.

findings.description: The fault test can observe status low at injection and still miss a high level during the preceding reset. CON-SUP-109 and this item require the full, uninterrupted low interval.
findings.requested_change: Cover reset assertion and the pre-software interval as well as the startup fault interval in the status verification.

findings.description: The item excludes a period whose control cycle starts before checks pass. CON-SUP-107 bars early task release but does not rule out a scheduled release later in that same cycle. CON-SUP-101 and CON-SUP-102 leave that alignment and the first T_DIAG release phase open.
findings.requested_change: Define the first counted window and latest alive detection point for each task using the approved startup and release alignment.

findings.description: A preempted task can use less processor time than its CON-SUP-103 limit while exceeding the same limit in elapsed time. The no-overrun outcome depends on the measurement basis left open in OP-SYS-013.
findings.requested_change: Use the approved execution-time basis for the no-overrun rule and include a preempted execution in the boundary checks.

findings.description: The 12 ms expiry is referenced to a previous refresh, leaving no expiry reference if the window watchdog becomes active and its first refresh never occurs. That case matters to the fallback reset in STK-SUP-005.
findings.requested_change: Define the activation event and the interval that governs expiry before the first accepted refresh.

findings.description: This item requires all detected faults in history, while SYS-DIAG-010 allows entry as late as the first transmitted bit. A query or reset between detection and entry yields different history outcomes. CON-SUP-110 and CON-SUP-113 leave that interval open.
findings.requested_change: Set a single history membership event and define the expected query and retained contents before entry and after an intervening reset.

findings.description: The proposed test sets reset flags and checks that classification follows the flags. CON-SUP-111 names five classes but gives no expected mapping or precedence for combined flags or flags retained from an earlier reset.
findings.requested_change: Reference the approved classification rule and give expected classes for single, combined and retained flag patterns.

findings.description: The text requires detection at the exact execution-limit expiry. The rationale says exact declaration is infeasible and proposes an unapproved tolerance. The measurement resolution in CON-SUP-103 does not supply that tolerance.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the permitted latency from expiry and apply the same declaration bound in the requirement and verification.

findings.description: This item declares an overrun when execution is incomplete at expiry, while SYS-SUP-007 forbids one for a completion measured at or below the limit. With a mapping left open by OP-SYS-027, a completion just after expiry can meet both conditions.
findings.requested_change: Use a consistent basis for expiry and the no-overrun decision, and verify completion at expiry and just after it when the observation maps to the limit.

findings.description: With truncation and a 2 ms limit, a start at 2.05 ms can be measured at 2.0 ms and be accepted by this item. CON-SUP-103 classifies a start later than the limit as late. OP-SYS-027 has not resolved how the measurement maps times near the limit.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the mapping of actual start times to the measured boundary and verify a start immediately beyond the limit against the approved interpretation.

findings.description: This demonstration checks for the presence of the CON-SUP-111 startup message. Without a defined message identity, the procedure cannot distinguish that message from startup FLT or other simulated serial output.
findings.requested_change: Use the approved startup-message identity to define what the simulated serial capture must contain.

findings.description: When equally timed faults straddle the eight-report cutoff, either report can be displaced under the current wording. CON-SUP-113 gives the count but leaves the tie unresolved, changing the GET FAULTS result.
findings.requested_change: Specify how equally timed reports are ordered at the cutoff and verify which report is retained.

findings.description: From the eighth detection onward this item changes required history membership at detection, while SYS-DIAG-010 allows later entry. A query or reset before entry leaves both the new and the displaced report unresolved under CON-SUP-110 and CON-SUP-113.
findings.requested_change: Use the approved history membership event to define the retained set on each side of that event and after an intervening reset.

findings.description: The ordering applies only if the startup failure leads to a software reset request. A watchdog active during startup can reset after the failing computation and before either reporting or the request. CON-SUP-106 and CON-SUP-107 give no timing basis that excludes this case.
findings.requested_change: Resolve startup watchdog operation and define how the report sequence is preserved or handled if expiry intervenes.

findings.description: The continuous CON-SUP-109 and CON-SUP-110 hold includes reset assertion and the interval before software acts. CON-SUP-003 gives no pin or board evidence that both outputs remain driven low, and sampled simulator values cannot establish the whole interval.
findings.requested_change: Establish the pin and board behavior for the reset paths and plan verification that covers the complete low-output interval.

findings.description: The latched status hold spans each reset, but CON-SUP-003 gives no external pin behavior during reset or before software configures it. A simulator result showing no high sample does not establish continuous low status over that interval.
findings.requested_change: Establish how the external status level is held low through the reset paths and verify the complete hold interval.

findings.description: The only history-entry deadline is the first transmitted bit. A watchdog reset that prevents transmission from starting leaves no expected history outcome. CON-SUP-110 requires survival of the history across that reset, and OP-SYS-015 leaves entry of the detected fault open.
findings.requested_change: Specify whether the report must appear when reset prevents transmission from starting and verify that case.

findings.description: The first-bit reset test reads GET FAULTS only after restart. Startup can reconstruct the report from separately retained data even when the history entry was incomplete at the first bit. The test cannot distinguish retention under CON-SUP-110 from the required entry order.
findings.requested_change: Observe durable history-entry completion and the first transmitted bit on a common time base. Verify the post-reset outcome separately.

findings.description: The valid-start test treats absence of a first release as failure. CON-SUP-107 and this item impose a release gate and give no deadline for a release. A run with no release cannot exercise the ordering comparison.
findings.requested_change: Classify a run without a release as inconclusive for the ordering check, or judge missing release against a separately sourced startup progression requirement.

findings.description: The timing test equates full-pass completion with processing the segment ending at __app_end without a fault. A pass that skips an earlier segment can satisfy that criterion while violating the full-image obligation in CON-SUP-108 and SYS-MEM-007.
findings.requested_change: Count completion only when the pass trace shows full image coverage, and apply the 11 s bounds to those verified completion events.

findings.description: The supplementary test requires code 7 on the line in the cycle that processed the corrupt segment. CON-SUP-105 anchors detection to completion of the failing computation, OP-SYS-005 leaves the integrity method open, and CON-SUP-112 allows serial transmission within 10 ms of detection.
findings.requested_change: Verify segment cadence using the range trace, and judge diagnostic timing from the failing computation applicable to the selected integrity method.

findings.description: CON-SUP-110 orders safe-state entry before report transmission. SYS-WDG-007 can withhold a refresh and trigger the CON-SUP-106 reset before either event. The item has no outcome for this preemption.
findings.requested_change: Apply the approved watchdog precedence and give a verdict for a reset before safe-state entry or the start of transmission.

findings.description: The text prohibits output rises 'between' the CON-SUP-105 event and the next reset. The rationale rejects a rise at the event itself. These readings give different verdicts for a coincident low-to-high transition.
findings.requested_change: State explicitly whether the prohibition includes the fault event and where it ends at reset, using the same endpoints in verification.

findings.description: The text prohibits a status rise 'between' the CON-SUP-105 event and the next reset, while the rationale rejects a rise at the event itself. A coincident transition has different verdicts under the text and test.
findings.requested_change: State the inclusion rule for the fault event and the reset boundary explicitly in the requirement and test.

findings.description: The proposed comparison uses the first measured value above the limit as the reference for a future detection deadline. OP-SYS-025 asks for a decision from configured limit expiry. CON-SUP-103 quantization can separate those events and cause the test to accept an overdue declaration.
findings.requested_change: Record limit expiry and measured crossing separately, and trace the comparison to the approved origin for any separate declaration deadline.

findings.description: The sweep accepts multiples of 100 µs if two values are 100 µs apart. An output alternating between 0 and 100 µs regardless of injected delay passes, although CON-SUP-103 requires measuring the delay from release to start.
findings.requested_change: Verify that the readout tracks the injected release-to-start interval as well as its increment, and apply the approved mapping when it is available.

findings.description: CON-SUP-104 and CON-SUP-105 put the flow check and fault event at cycle end. OP-SYS-036 leaves receipt at the same instant undecided, so the same trace can yield an arrived checkpoint or a flow fault.
findings.requested_change: Resolve receipt-versus-evaluation precedence at the boundary and apply it to the coincident-receipt test.

findings.description: The multiple-of-100 µs and one-pair criteria can pass values unrelated to execution time or measured from the wrong start event. They do not verify the start-to-completion or start-to-expiry intervals required by this item and grounded in CON-SUP-103.
findings.requested_change: Compare the readout with independently observed execution intervals in completion and overrun runs, applying the approved time basis and quantization.

findings.description: Analysis criterion (d) forbids carrying prior-cycle count or order state into evaluation. CON-SUP-104 limits what can affect the result. Retained cycle-tagged state can be ignored before it influences evaluation and still fail criterion (d).
findings.requested_change: Require evidence that every retained state path leaves current-cycle presence, count and order unaffected by prior-cycle checkpoints.

findings.description: The nominal run observes a status edge and the three failure runs observe status held low. All four can pass if the valid path drives status high before the checks finish and the injected-failure paths suppress the edge. That evidence does not establish the CON-SUP-109 ordering.
findings.requested_change: Observe successful completion of every startup check and the status edge on a common time base in the nominal run, and compare their order.

findings.description: The item mandates 11 s of continuous high status from the status edge. CON-SUP-108 gives 11 s for a full runtime integrity pass with a different origin. STK-SUP-015 and CON-SUP-116 give no high-status demonstration duration.
findings.requested_change: Use the approved demonstration duration and timing origin in this item and its dependent cases.

findings.description: An absent FLT prefix does not establish absence of declarations. A late fault can leave a partial prefix after the high-status observation ends, or the capture can close before the prefix completes under a start-of-transmission interpretation of CON-SUP-112. A subsequent service reply and an alive positive-control run can still pass.
findings.requested_change: Use capture and frame criteria that cover the approved report deadline and account for truncation. Observe declarations directly where the verdict claims their absence.

findings.description: The observation ends at a complete code 5 report, but the run does not establish an otherwise valid startup or define the verdict if the report never arrives. A configuration fault can hold status low and mask the CON-SUP-107 code-integrity case.
findings.requested_change: Isolate the code-integrity failure in an otherwise valid setup and define a finite observation with a complete code 5 report required to pass.

findings.description: The run does not establish an intact code image or define a verdict if no code 6 report arrives. A code-integrity failure can keep status low without exercising the configuration-integrity check in CON-SUP-107.
findings.requested_change: Use an intact application image, isolate the configuration-integrity failure and require a complete code 6 report within a defined observation interval.

findings.description: The run does not establish that both integrity checks can pass with the range-fault stimulus. A change invalidating the stored CRC can produce code 6, keeping status low without exercising CON-SUP-115. There is no finite observation criterion when code 9 is absent.
findings.requested_change: Define a range-fault stimulus that preserves application and configuration integrity, and require a complete code 9 report within a defined observation interval.

findings.description: The threshold of 1099 complete cycles assumes the first cycle begins within 10 ms of the status edge. CON-SUP-101 and CON-SUP-109 specify the cycle and the signal without bounding the interval between these events.
findings.requested_change: Derive the count from approved first-cycle alignment and observation duration, or anchor observation to a recorded cycle boundary.

findings.description: Completion is due by the execution-limit expiry of each scheduled release. A task that is never released or never starts has no execution-limit expiry under SYS-SUP-003. The criterion leaves that missing CON-SUP-101 slot without a finite failure verdict.
findings.requested_change: Enumerate the expected release slots independently of observed releases and define finite failure criteria for missing release or start before checking completion deadlines.

findings.description: The threshold of 1098 refreshes inherits the unapproved first-cycle delay in SYS-TEST-010. CON-SUP-106 gives cycle-end and inter-refresh rules but no count measured from the status edge.
findings.requested_change: Use the approved cycle and observation alignment to derive a count, or judge refreshes against the observed eligible cycle ends.

findings.description: The count and 6–12 ms spacing can pass for refreshes displaced from cycle ends or with a missed refresh at one cycle end and an extra refresh elsewhere. The test does not establish the once-per-cycle end-of-cycle service in CON-SUP-106.
findings.requested_change: Associate refreshes with eligible cycle ends and check both the required service per cycle and the observed inter-refresh intervals.

findings.description: The interval that 'contains no refresh' has ambiguous endpoints. With inclusive endpoints, refreshes exactly 100 ms apart can satisfy the text even though SYS-WDG-004 requires a gap shorter than the CON-SUP-106 timeout.
findings.requested_change: Define the leading, trailing and inter-refresh interval boundaries and give an explicit verdict for a gap of exactly 100 ms.

findings.description: The demonstration mandates a line feed though CON-SUP-113 does not specify one for STS. CON-SUP-112 specifies it for FLT. The demonstration also accepts a bare STS prefix and line feed without the two fields required by CON-SUP-113.
findings.requested_change: Verify that the response contains both fields and remove the unsupported terminator from the pass criteria pending approved response framing.

findings.description: The item selects the end of the request as the time origin and leaves the response endpoint open. OP-SYS-007 records the CON-SUP-113 timing references as undecided. A response that begins before the deadline and ends after it has no unique verdict.
findings.requested_change: Apply the approved request and response timing reference events to the demonstration.

findings.description: The 40 ms derivation assumes T_IN periods are already progressing at injection. An offset of 100 ms from the status edge does not establish that condition under CON-SUP-101 or CON-SUP-102. OP-SYS-020 leaves first-cycle alignment open, so the test can reject a controller that satisfies the alive rule.
findings.requested_change: Qualify the injection against observed T_IN period boundaries in a separate positive-control run and derive its deadline from the resulting alive-window expiry and approved report endpoint.

findings.description: The refresh cutoff uses physical start-limit expiry while SYS-SUP-002 declares lateness from the first measured value above the limit. If a refresh falls between those events, the duty to refresh can depend on whether the task later starts before the measured crossing.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the late-start mapping and define a cutoff that can be evaluated at the refresh instant. Use the same cutoff in SYS-WDG-007.

findings.description: Fault-free run V1 accepts a refresh anywhere between successive cycle boundaries after the flow check. It can pass alternating early and late refreshes outside the CON-SUP-106 window and does not establish end-of-cycle service.
findings.requested_change: Verify the relationship between cycle end, flow-check completion and refresh, and check spacing against the 6–12 ms window.

findings.description: The inclusive prohibition can yield a CON-SUP-106 watchdog reset 12 ms after the previous refresh. This can interrupt the CON-SUP-110 report-then-software-reset sequence and does not count as a supervisor reset for the latch.
findings.requested_change: Apply the approved precedence for watchdog reset, reporting and software reset, including the effect on the latch sequence.

findings.description: The prohibition includes refresh coincident with cutoff. V3 places expiry strictly before or after the reference refresh, and neither the additional overrun run nor the cycle-boundary runs establish that a refresh would otherwise fall exactly at cutoff. An implementation that prohibits refresh only strictly after cutoff can pass.
findings.requested_change: Add a valid case or analysis that distinguishes a refresh at cutoff from one immediately before it.

findings.description: STK-SUP-003 requires detection when a task is skipped. SYS-SUP-005 assigns a checkpoint to the cycle in which its task was released. If a scheduled release never occurs, this assignment gives the cycle no checkpoint for that task. The missing-checkpoint rule then leaves open whether to declare a flow fault at that cycle end.
findings.requested_change: Define the expected checkpoint set independently of observed releases and specify the end-of-cycle verdict when a scheduled release never occurs. Verify that case separately from a release whose checkpoint fails to arrive.

findings.description: A configuration block can present both a failed CRC and an out-of-range value under CON-SUP-107 and CON-SUP-115. SYS-RST-012 requires a software reset for the integrity fault and SYS-RST-003 requires a latch for the range fault. OP-SYS-040 records the unresolved validity and precedence of the two checks.
findings.requested_change: Apply the approved precedence to the startup checks, fault reports, history and recovery behavior when both conditions are observable.

findings.description: After the CON-SUP-110 latch survives a reset and startup checks pass, SYS-SAFE-010 and SYS-SAFE-011 hold the signals low. SYS-MEM-004, SYS-SUP-001 and SYS-MEM-005 through SYS-MEM-008 still lack a common rule for which application and supervision functions run in that mode.
findings.requested_change: Apply the approved retained-latch mode rule to application releases, supervision, runtime integrity checking, diagnostics and watchdog service.

findings.description: CON-SUP-110 counts supervisor resets with the same fault code. SYS-RST-001 starts the reset deadline from the first operational fault, and SYS-RST-013 orders the report of the fault that causes the reset. When two distinct codes are reported before one reset, the set leaves the code attributed to that reset undefined, so the next startup can produce different latch counts.
findings.requested_change: Record and resolve which fault code is attributed to a supervisor reset when multiple faults precede it. Apply the rule to the reset sequence and verify a mixed-code case.

findings.description: The startup message, fault reports and service replies share the CON-SUP-007 serial line. As OP-SYS-042 shows, a GET FAULTS response can occupy the line for longer than the CON-SUP-112 fault-report budget. The set still leaves frame handling, admitted simultaneous reports and service deadline precedence undecided.
findings.requested_change: Apply the agreed traffic and frame-handling rules, then check the admitted frame lengths and concurrent traffic against both diagnostic deadlines.

findings.description: The producer of the CON-SUP-107 block and the checker in SYS-MEM-002 can use identical CRC parameters and still disagree if they serialize fields differently or include different bytes. OP-SYS-005 now records these interface decisions, and the contract remains undefined.
findings.requested_change: Reference the approved serialized block layout, covered bytes and treatment of the stored CRC field. Supply reference blocks for independent verification.

findings.description: SYS-SAFE-007 and SYS-SAFE-008 direct readers to SYS-SAFE-003 for the latched hold under CON-SUP-110 and CON-SUP-115. SYS-SAFE-010 and SYS-SAFE-011 own those holds. SYS-RST-012 points to SYS-RST-002 for report completion before a reset request, which SYS-RST-013 owns. SYS-RST-013 also points to SYS-WDG-005 for window-watchdog refresh cessation, now owned by SYS-WDG-007.
findings.requested_change: Update the rationales to cite the requirements that own the current hold, report ordering and window-watchdog cessation rules.

findings.description: SYS-WDG-006 now accepts a refresh at exactly 12 ms, resolving the boundary verdict. For a missing refresh, its W2 test delegates the latest reset time to an upper limit chosen in design. The rationale of SYS-WDG-007 still says the reset occurs at exactly 12 ms. These give different timing criteria for the same CON-SUP-106 timeout.
findings.requested_change: Define a common timeout and latest reset criterion for the no-refresh case while preserving acceptance of a refresh at exactly 12 ms. Use the same criterion in the watchdog rationales and W2. Record an open point if timing tolerance needs approval.

findings.description: OP-SYS-009 says a service request received after safe-state entry cannot be answered within 50 ms when a software reset follows within 20 ms. CON-SUP-110 and CON-SUP-113 give maximum intervals. A short reply can fit before some allowed reset times, and a longer reply or one received nearer the reset may be interrupted.
findings.requested_change: Assess the available service time against the actual reset sequence and permitted reply lengths. Use that assessment to frame the pending decision on accepted requests and their outcomes.

findings.description: OP-SYS-043 identifies evidence methods for CON-SUP-110 retention. The target and Renode reset behavior, startup handling of retained state, and validity of latch, history and reset-sequence records after an interrupted update still lack evidence or an agreed recovery rule.
findings.requested_change: Obtain the identified platform and simulator evidence and apply an approved interrupted-update recovery rule to the retained state requirements.

findings.description: OP-SYS-038 is marked nonblocking even though SYS-TEST-015 says its undecided stimulus can prevent any valid alive positive-control run under CON-SUP-116. SYS-TEST-001 and SYS-WDG-006 also remain proposed despite depending on the blocking message-format and first-refresh decisions in OP-SYS-002 and OP-SYS-010.
findings.requested_change: Align blocking flags and affected-item statuses with the decisions that can prevent a required demonstration or change a required outcome. Identify which remaining observation choices can be deferred.

findings.description: The reworked test rejects a run masked by an earlier timing or flow fault. It still identifies no admitted CON-SUP-116 stimulus that can suppress T_IN completion for two periods without a competing fault under SYS-SUP-003 or SYS-SUP-005. Reporting all such runs as not run leaves SYS-TEST-006 without its stated positive control.
findings.requested_change: Establish a feasible non-masking stimulus or an approved alternative that isolates alive supervision, and carry that approach into the positive-control criteria.

findings.description: SYS-TEST-011 now has finite failure criteria for missing release and missing start. If OP-SYS-013 selects task processor time under CON-SUP-103, a task that starts and is then indefinitely preempted never reaches execution-limit expiry. The completion criterion gives that nominal run no finite verdict.
findings.requested_change: Define a finite demonstration outcome for a started task that never completes or reaches execution-limit expiry. Keep that outcome consistent with the approved execution-time basis and the alive rule.

findings.description: The independent-watchdog refresh obligation holds whenever no listed task fault has become detectable since reset. That includes startup and retained-latch operation, where CON-SUP-106 gives no service or first-interval policy.
findings.requested_change: Specify the approved watchdog service modes and the event anchoring the first refresh interval.

findings.description: SYS-WDG-005 and SYS-WDG-007 stop both watchdog services at the same task-fault cutoff. A watchdog already near its CON-SUP-106 expiry can reset the controller ahead of the report and software reset required by CON-SUP-110 and CON-SUP-112.
findings.requested_change: Apply the approved precedence to the independent-watchdog cessation rule and its interaction with the window watchdog, reporting and software reset.

findings.description: The CON-SUP-110 latch rule still leaves the effect of an intervening watchdog or other reset undefined. The rationale describes fault-free operation after successful startup, and the normative text gives no event that starts the 60 s interval.
findings.requested_change: Define the intervening events that break the sequence and the approved start event for the 60 s interval.

findings.description: CON-SUP-111 requires a startup message carrying the reset cause. The framing and encoding remain open, so a verifier cannot identify the message or decode the classified cause.
findings.requested_change: Reference the approved startup-message format and the expected encoding for each reset class.

findings.description: CON-SUP-111 requires the service tool to read the latest reset cause. CON-SUP-113 defines no cause field in either supported response and specifies ERR for other requests. The interaction that satisfies both decisions remains open.
findings.requested_change: Specify the approved service-tool interaction for retrieving the cause and reconcile it with the CON-SUP-113 protocol.

findings.description: The CON-SUP-112 phrase 'within 10 ms' leaves the observable endpoint open. The rationale selects completion of the line feed while OP-SYS-007 still treats start versus completion of transmission as undecided.
findings.requested_change: Use the approved observable endpoint in both the requirement and its verification.

findings.description: The item requires a CON-SUP-112 report for each detected fault. SYS-WDG-007 and SYS-WDG-006 can reset the controller before the report starts or completes. The item gives no approved report outcome when that reset preempts transmission.
findings.requested_change: Apply the approved watchdog precedence and specify the required report outcome for reset before or during transmission.

findings.description: SYS-DIAG-003 assigns code 8 to a watchdog reset and SYS-DIAG-002 requires an entity field. The task names, CODE and CONFIG listed in CON-SUP-112 give no value for that code.
findings.requested_change: Specify the approved entity field for a watchdog-reset report.

findings.description: The entity for a flow fault is the affected supervised task. One CON-SUP-104 evaluation can find several missing or out-of-order checkpoints. The set gives no rule for selecting the task name required by CON-SUP-112 in that case.
findings.requested_change: Specify which task name is reported for each approved single- and multiple-checkpoint fault case.

findings.description: CON-SUP-112 says milliseconds since start without defining the reference event. SYS-DIAG-005 selects the latest reset and says 'the controller started' without an observable event. OP-SYS-007 leaves that origin undecided.
findings.requested_change: Define the timestamp origin using the approved observable event and apply it consistently after the relevant reset classes.

findings.description: CON-SUP-113 supplies the STS template. The request boundary, allowed state values and fault-count meaning remain open, so a verifier cannot form an agreed complete request and predict its response for a known state and fault history.
findings.requested_change: Specify the approved request framing, state encoding and fault-count semantics.

findings.description: The 50 ms limit in CON-SUP-113 gives no agreed measurement events for receipt or transmission. A reply that starts inside 50 ms and finishes later has no unique verdict.
findings.requested_change: Define the approved observable request and response events for timing GET STATUS.

findings.description: The CON-SUP-113 GET FAULTS response has no agreed wire order or completion framing. A verifier cannot distinguish a complete response with fewer than eight reports, including an empty history, from an incomplete transmission.
findings.requested_change: Specify the approved report order, framing and completion indication for zero through eight reports.

findings.description: The 50 ms limit in CON-SUP-113 gives no agreed start event or endpoint for a multi-record reply. A transmission can begin inside the limit and finish outside it.
findings.requested_change: Define the approved timing events for GET FAULTS, including responses with zero or multiple records.

findings.description: The GET FAULTS trigger has no mode qualification. A CON-SUP-110 reset can interrupt an accepted request, and the set leaves request acceptance and response behavior in the latched safe state open.
findings.requested_change: Define the approved acceptance and response behavior during pending reset and retained-latch operation, including reset during an accepted response.

findings.description: CON-SUP-113 requires ERR for other requests. The recognition boundary and finite response observation window remain open, so a test cannot determine when it sent a complete unrecognized request or when a missing ERR fails.
findings.requested_change: Define the approved framing for recognizing an unrecognized request and the observable deadline for its ERR response.

findings.description: CON-SUP-114 measures processor use at the configured core clock. The item gives neither the clock setting nor a controlled simulator configuration that supplies it, leaving the measurement conditions unreproducible.
findings.requested_change: Reference the approved core-clock setting or controlled simulator configuration.

findings.description: CON-SUP-115 requires rejection of an unknown task. CON-SUP-101 names the default tasks, and the approved set of supported identifiers remains undefined. A verifier cannot determine the verdict for an identifier outside the default configuration.
findings.requested_change: Reference the approved supported identifier set and use it to select known and unknown values for verification.

findings.description: STK-SUP-007 and CON-SUP-107 identify the image and when to check it. The integrity criterion and reference needed to establish an independent expected verdict for a test image remain open.
findings.requested_change: Reference the approved integrity criterion and reference information used to determine the expected result for each image.

findings.description: CON-SUP-107 supplies the CRC-32 polynomial. Different initialization, reflection and final XOR settings can give different values for the same covered bytes while using that polynomial.
findings.requested_change: Reference the complete approved CRC-32 parameters and identify an independently reproducible check value.

findings.description: Under CON-SUP-106, withholding the refresh after a flow fault at the end of a nominal 10 ms cycle can leave about 2 ms before window-watchdog expiry. The resulting hardware reset can preempt the CON-SUP-110 software reset request and keep that incident out of the supervisor-reset latch count.
findings.requested_change: Specify the approved reset outcome, timing and latch-count treatment when hardware expiry competes with the software reset request.

findings.description: If a watchdog is active during the CON-SUP-107 startup checks, the time left after a failing computation may be insufficient for the CON-SUP-110 report and reset sequence. The startup watchdog policy and timing evidence remain open.
findings.requested_change: Establish the approved startup watchdog policy and the time available for reporting and requesting reset after the failing computation.

findings.description: The item orders completion of the terminating line feed before a software reset request. If the CON-SUP-106 window watchdog resets first, the ordering condition need never be exercised even though the CON-SUP-110 and CON-SUP-112 report is interrupted.
findings.requested_change: Define the approved report outcome when a hardware reset preempts the intended software reset request.

findings.description: The test must establish both outputs low from any reset under CON-SUP-109. CON-SUP-003 and CON-SUP-005 give no evidence that the simulator represents external output levels during reset assertion and before software configures the pins.
findings.requested_change: Use approved evidence that covers both external outputs through reset and software takeover for every applicable reset path.

findings.description: CON-SUP-109 requires status low from any reset, including a reset taken while SYS-SAFE-006 has status high. The stated test lacks evidence of the pin level during reset assertion and before software acts.
findings.requested_change: Establish how to verify the external status level through reset assertion and software takeover for every applicable reset path.

findings.description: The startup fault test checks that neither output is high at any recorded sample. CON-SUP-109 and SYS-SAFE-007 require the uninterrupted low interval from reset. A trace that begins after software starts can miss the reset interval and early output transitions.
findings.requested_change: Combine the injected-fault test with evidence that covers both outputs throughout reset and every interval the simulator trace cannot observe.

findings.description: The sampled status trace can show low at startup fault detection while missing a high level during the preceding reset or before the first sample. CON-SUP-109 and SYS-SAFE-008 require the full low interval.
findings.requested_change: Cover reset assertion and the pre-software interval in addition to the sampled startup-fault interval.

findings.description: The rationale assumes a control cycle that starts before startup checks pass cannot contain a scheduled release after the checks pass. CON-SUP-107 bars early release, and CON-SUP-101 and CON-SUP-102 leave that cycle alignment and the first T_DIAG release phase unspecified.
findings.requested_change: Define the first counted period and latest initial alive detection point for each task using the approved startup and release alignment.

findings.description: A preempted task can use less processor time than its CON-SUP-103 execution limit while exceeding that limit in elapsed time. The no-overrun verdict depends on the measurement basis still open in OP-SYS-013.
findings.requested_change: Apply the approved execution-time basis and verify the boundary with a preempted execution.

findings.description: The timeout uses the previous refresh as its reference. If the watchdog is active and its first refresh never occurs, the item gives no expiry reference for the CON-SUP-106 fallback reset required by STK-SUP-005.
findings.requested_change: Define the activation event and the expiry interval that apply before the first accepted refresh.

findings.description: SYS-DIAG-006 requires all reports in history from detection while fewer than eight faults have occurred. SYS-DIAG-010 allows entry as late as the first transmitted bit. A GET FAULTS query or reset between detection and entry yields incompatible expected histories under CON-SUP-110 and CON-SUP-113.
findings.requested_change: Use one approved history-membership event and define query results and retained content on both sides of it.

findings.description: The planned test sets reset flags and checks that the classification follows the flags. CON-SUP-111 names five classes and provides no mapping or precedence for combined flags or flags retained from an earlier reset.
findings.requested_change: Reference the approved classification rule and give expected classes for single, combined and retained flag patterns.

findings.description: The text requires declaration at the exact execution-limit expiry. Its rationale says exact declaration is infeasible and its verification uses a tolerance awaiting approval. The measurement resolution in CON-SUP-103 supplies no declaration tolerance.
findings.requested_change: Apply the approved declaration latency from expiry in both the normative requirement and its verification.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-003 declares an overrun when execution is incomplete at expiry. SYS-SUP-007 forbids it for a completion measured at or below the limit. A completion just after expiry can satisfy both conditions if the CON-SUP-103 measurement maps it to the limit.
findings.requested_change: Use a consistent approved basis for expiry and the no-overrun rule. Verify completion at expiry and just after expiry with a measured value at the limit.

findings.description: With truncation, a task starting 2.05 ms after release can measure 2.0 ms and satisfy the no-fault rule. CON-SUP-103 classifies a start later than its configured limit as late. OP-SYS-027 leaves that boundary mapping unresolved.
findings.requested_change: Apply the approved mapping of actual start times to the measured boundary and verify a start immediately beyond the limit.

findings.description: The demonstration checks for the SYS-RST-009 startup message. With the CON-SUP-111 message identity unresolved, the serial capture cannot distinguish it from a startup fault report or other output.
findings.requested_change: Use the approved startup-message identity and encoding to define what the capture must contain.

findings.description: When faults with the same detection instant straddle the eight-report cutoff, either tied report can be displaced. CON-SUP-113 fixes the count and leaves the tie unresolved, which changes the result returned by GET FAULTS.
findings.requested_change: Apply the approved ordering of equally timed reports and verify which report is retained at the cutoff.

findings.description: From the eighth detection onward, SYS-DIAG-011 changes required membership at detection. SYS-DIAG-010 permits entry by the first transmitted bit. A query or reset before entry leaves both the new report and the displaced report unresolved under CON-SUP-110 and CON-SUP-113.
findings.requested_change: Apply the approved history-membership event and define the retained set before entry, after entry and after an intervening reset.

findings.description: The ordering applies when the failing startup check causes a software reset request. A watchdog active during startup can reset after the failing computation and before either reporting or the request. CON-SUP-106 and CON-SUP-107 give no timing basis that excludes this sequence.
findings.requested_change: Resolve startup watchdog operation and define how the report sequence is handled if watchdog expiry intervenes.

findings.description: The continuous latched hold under CON-SUP-109 and CON-SUP-110 includes reset assertion and the interval before software acts. CON-SUP-003 provides no pin or board evidence that both outputs remain driven low, and simulator samples cannot establish those intervals without model evidence.
findings.requested_change: Establish pin and board behavior for the applicable reset paths and use evidence covering the full hold interval.

findings.description: The latched status hold spans every intervening reset. CON-SUP-003 gives no external status-pin behavior during reset or before GPIO setup. A simulator trace showing no high sample cannot establish continuous low status across those intervals.
findings.requested_change: Establish how the external status level stays low across reset and verify the complete hold interval.

findings.description: The only entry deadline is the first transmitted bit. If a watchdog reset prevents transmission from starting, that deadline never occurs. CON-SUP-110 requires retention across watchdog reset and OP-SYS-015 leaves the outcome for the detected fault open.
findings.requested_change: Specify whether a report must appear in history when reset prevents transmission from starting and verify that case.

findings.description: CON-SUP-110 orders safe-state entry before report transmission. Under SYS-WDG-007 and CON-SUP-106, expiry can reset the controller before either event. The item gives no required outcome for that preemption.
findings.requested_change: Apply the approved precedence and define the safe-state and report verdict when a hardware reset occurs first.

findings.description: CON-SUP-104 and CON-SUP-105 place evaluation and the flow fault event at cycle end. SYS-SUP-005 leaves receipt coincident with that boundary to OP-SYS-036, so the same trace can yield an arrived checkpoint or a missing-checkpoint fault.
findings.requested_change: Apply the approved receipt-versus-evaluation precedence to the normative rule and the coincident-receipt test.

findings.description: The 11 s high-status interval remains a normative demonstration target starting at the status edge. CON-SUP-108 supplies 11 s for a runtime integrity pass with a different origin. STK-SUP-015 and CON-SUP-116 supply no demonstration duration.
findings.requested_change: Apply the approved demonstration duration and timing origin to this item and its dependent demonstrations.

findings.description: The reworked CON-SUP-107 code-integrity demonstration isolates its stimulus and requires a complete code 5 line. If the check never finishes and no reset or report occurs, the fallback observation limit still depends on an undefined maximum startup duration.
findings.requested_change: Give the no-reset, no-report case a finite observation limit tied to the approved startup timing.

findings.description: The reworked CON-SUP-107 configuration-integrity demonstration isolates its stimulus and requires a complete code 6 line. If the CRC check never finishes and no reset or report occurs, the fallback observation limit still depends on an undefined maximum startup duration.
findings.requested_change: Give the no-reset, no-report case a finite observation limit tied to the approved startup timing.

findings.description: The reworked CON-SUP-115 range-fault stimulus preserves the CRC. The test ends relative to the fault's detectability instant or an undefined startup limit. If an implementation never performs the range check or reports code 9, the test still has no finite failure point.
findings.requested_change: Define a finite observation bound that applies even if the range-check event and report never occur.

findings.description: The 1099-cycle minimum still assumes the first cycle begins within 10 ms of the status edge. CON-SUP-101 and CON-SUP-109 specify the cycle and the signal without bounding the interval between them. Marking the count as a proposal leaves its acceptance verdict unresolved.
findings.requested_change: Derive the minimum from approved alignment and duration, or anchor the observation interval to a recorded cycle boundary and derive the count from that interval.

findings.description: The reworked demonstration associates refreshes with eligible cycles and checks spacing. It still accepts a refresh anywhere after flow-check completion and before the next cycle end. A fixed 9 ms delay on every 10 ms cycle can pass those checks without establishing CON-SUP-106 cycle-end service.
findings.requested_change: Define an acceptance criterion for the time from cycle end to its associated refresh, and record the needed decision if the allowed delay is unspecified.

findings.description: The unsupported line-feed requirement is removed. The revised criterion still accepts at least one character from each field without establishing that the CON-SUP-113 STS response is complete. A reset or truncation after the first character of a longer fault-count field can pass.
findings.requested_change: Require a complete response in the demonstration and reference the approved SYS-DIAG-007 field and framing rules for identifying it.

findings.description: The item selects the end of the request as the 50 ms origin and leaves the response endpoint open. OP-SYS-007 records both CON-SUP-113 timing references as undecided.
findings.requested_change: Apply the approved request and response measurement events to the demonstration.

findings.description: The watchdog cutoff is physical start-limit expiry for a late release. SYS-SUP-002 classifies the release at measured crossing under CON-SUP-103. If a refresh falls between the two, its eligibility can depend on whether the task subsequently starts before the measured crossing.
findings.requested_change: Use an approved late-start mapping and define a cutoff that can be evaluated at the refresh instant. Apply it consistently to both watchdogs.

findings.description: V1 now measures refresh order and 6–12 ms spacing. It still permits any steady delay between cycle end and the next cycle end. SYS-WDG-008 limits the change in delay across cycles, so it also accepts a steady 9 ms delay and supplies no verdict for the CON-SUP-106 cycle-end obligation.
findings.requested_change: Add an independently checkable cycle-end-to-refresh criterion to V1. Base it on the approved meaning of cycle-end service and retain the separate inter-refresh check.

findings.description: The inclusive refresh prohibition can trigger a CON-SUP-106 window-watchdog reset before the CON-SUP-110 report and software reset request. That hardware reset can interrupt the report and does not contribute to the same-code supervisor-reset latch sequence.
findings.requested_change: Apply the approved precedence for watchdog expiry, reporting and software reset, including its effect on the latch sequence.

findings.description: SYS-CFG-001 takes task periods from the configuration block. SYS-SUP-001 and SYS-SUP-005 depend on the configured release schedule, but the release rules in SYS-CFG-003 and SYS-CFG-009 cover the defaults only. The set leaves it unclear whether the timer-driven scheduler in CON-SUP-006 uses a changed period or whether only supervision uses it under STK-SUP-004.
findings.requested_change: Define which configured periods govern application releases and which govern supervision. Record any owner decision needed on the supported periods and use one defined release schedule for the alive and flow checks.

findings.description: A block can fail the CRC check under CON-SUP-107 and contain an out-of-range value under CON-SUP-115. SYS-RST-012 requires a software reset for the first fault and SYS-RST-003 requires a latch for the second. OP-SYS-040 leaves the validity and precedence of these checks open.
findings.requested_change: Apply the approved check order and define the resulting report, history entry, reset and latch behavior when integrity and range checks can both fail.

findings.description: After a retained CON-SUP-110 latch and a successful startup, SYS-SAFE-010 and SYS-SAFE-011 hold the external signals low. SYS-MEM-004, SYS-SUP-001 and SYS-MEM-005 through SYS-MEM-008 lack a common rule for the application and supervision functions active in that state.
findings.requested_change: Apply the approved latched-state policy consistently to task releases, supervision, integrity checking, watchdog service, diagnostic service and fault handling.

findings.description: SYS-RST-004 now assigns the reset the code of the fault that starts the SYS-RST-001 deadline or triggers SYS-RST-012. Its rationale identifies this as an unapproved interpretation of CON-SUP-110. When two different faults precede one reset, that choice changes the next startup's latch count.
findings.requested_change: Use the approved fault-code attribution rule across reset timing, report ordering and latch counting. Update the mixed-code verification cases to exercise that rule.

findings.description: Startup messages, fault reports and service replies share the CON-SUP-007 line. An eight-report GET FAULTS response can occupy it longer than the CON-SUP-112 fault-report budget. Receipt of a fault during such a response has no agreed frame-handling or deadline precedence rule.
findings.requested_change: Define admitted simultaneous traffic, maximum frame lengths and the ordering or interruption of transmissions. Check that the resulting rules meet the approved report and service deadlines.

findings.description: The configuration producer and SYS-MEM-002 checker can use identical CRC parameters and still disagree about the bytes covered under CON-SUP-107. OP-SYS-005 leaves serialization, the covered range and treatment of the stored CRC field open.
findings.requested_change: Reference an approved producer-to-checker block format and include reference blocks with independently calculated expected CRC values.

findings.description: SYS-SAFE-007 and SYS-SAFE-008 cite SYS-SAFE-003 for the latched holds under CON-SUP-110 and CON-SUP-115, which SYS-SAFE-010 and SYS-SAFE-011 own. SYS-RST-012 cites SYS-RST-002 for report-before-reset ordering, which SYS-RST-013 owns. SYS-RST-013 cites SYS-WDG-005 for window-watchdog cessation, which SYS-WDG-007 owns.
findings.requested_change: Correct the rationale references to the requirements that state each hold, ordering or refresh obligation.

findings.description: The revised SYS-TEST-012 text requires a 6–12 ms interval from the preceding cycle's refresh for every included cycle. Its rationale checks only cycle association for the first cycle after startup if no prior refresh exists. The same first-refresh trace has different criteria, and CON-SUP-106 defines the window relative to a previous refresh.
findings.requested_change: Align the requirement and test on when a previous refresh is needed. Make the first-refresh verdict depend explicitly on the approved policy in OP-SYS-010.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-008 requires execution-time measurement only through completion or limit expiry, whichever comes first. SYS-SUP-007 forbids an overrun for a completed execution with a measured value at or below the limit. If the release finishes after expiry, substituting its last required sample at expiry for a completion measurement can suppress the CON-SUP-103 overrun.
findings.requested_change: Make the no-overrun comparison apply to a defined completion measurement and state how expiry takes precedence when measurement ends before completion. Exercise a release that finishes after expiry.

findings.description: OP-SYS-009 estimates the earliest software reset request at about 1.3 ms after safe-state entry using the longest default entity width for its shortest report. Under CON-SUP-007 and CON-SUP-112, a 13-character line with T_IN and a one-digit timestamp takes about 1.13 ms. The estimate also needs to distinguish the CON-SUP-110 reset request from the reset event that actually cuts off transmission.
findings.requested_change: Recalculate the service time ranges using the actual allowed frame lengths. State the assumptions about reset-request latency and identify the physical reset event used for the interruption verdict.

findings.description: OP-SYS-043 proposes evidence methods for CON-SUP-110 retention. The target and Renode reset behavior, startup handling of retained state and validity of the latch, history and reset-sequence records after an interrupted update remain unresolved.
findings.requested_change: Establish the retention and startup behavior for each covered reset path and define the recovery outcome for each interrupted update. Tie the planned test or analysis to those outcomes.

findings.description: The revised rationale fails a slot at the end of the following task period if it never completes. The requirement text still uses only execution-limit expiry. Under a processor-time interpretation of CON-SUP-103, an indefinitely preempted release may never reach expiry, and another release can complete in time to satisfy the SYS-SUP-001 alive rule.
findings.requested_change: Identify the finite observation rule as an explicit verification criterion and justify its applicability to each scheduled release. Record any approval needed for the completion expectation it adds.

findings.description: SYS-TEST-015 proposes withholding T_IN completion only from alive supervision so timing and flow remain valid under SYS-SUP-003 and SYS-SUP-005. OP-SYS-038 leaves that stimulus unapproved. Without an admitted isolating stimulus under CON-SUP-116, SYS-TEST-006 still lacks its stated positive control.
findings.requested_change: Apply the approved isolating stimulus and require evidence that alive supervision missed the completions while timing and flow remained valid through the end of the alive window.

findings.description: V2 cites suppressing T_IN releases as a possible way to isolate the alive cutoff. The revised SYS-SUP-005 makes each skipped scheduled release a missing checkpoint at its cycle end, so that stimulus produces an earlier flow fault. The SYS-WDG-003 rationale also omits the proposed alive-only stimulus now in SYS-TEST-015.
findings.requested_change: Remove release suppression as an isolating candidate and align V2 with the proposed or approved OP-SYS-038 stimulus. Require evidence that the alive rule alone makes the boundary refresh ineligible.

findings.description: CON-SUP-112 specifies milliseconds since start. The item selects the latest reset and refers to when the controller started without identifying an observable reference event. OP-SYS-007 leaves the origin open.
findings.requested_change: Use the approved observable timestamp origin and define the expected timestamp at the startup boundary.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-001 excludes a period whose control cycle starts before the startup checks pass. CON-SUP-107 prevents release before the checks pass but permits a later release in that same cycle under the scheduling information supplied. CON-SUP-101 and CON-SUP-102 leave startup alignment and the first T_DIAG release phase open.
findings.requested_change: Apply the approved first-period rule and T_DIAG phase, including the case where a cycle starts before startup checks pass and a release is scheduled after they pass.

findings.description: With truncation, a start 2.05 ms after release can measure 2.0 ms and satisfy the no-fault rule. CON-SUP-103 classifies starts later than the configured limit as late. OP-SYS-027 leaves the mapping near the limit open.
findings.requested_change: Apply the approved mapping and specify verdicts for starts exactly at the limit and immediately on either side of it.

findings.description: The 11 s high-status interval starts at the SYS-TEST-004 status edge. CON-SUP-108 gives 11 s for a runtime integrity pass with a different origin. STK-SUP-015 and CON-SUP-116 establish simulator testability, and the demonstration duration remains an author proposal.
findings.requested_change: Use the approved demonstration duration and origin, then align the dependent nominal-run criteria.

findings.description: The 1099-cycle minimum assumes the first complete cycle starts within 10 ms of the status edge. CON-SUP-101 defines the cycle duration and CON-SUP-109 defines the status signal. Neither establishes the relationship needed for this count.
findings.requested_change: Base the cycle count on approved cycle alignment and observation duration, or use an approved progression criterion with an independent observation origin.

findings.description: CON-SUP-112 leaves the endpoint of the 10 ms fault-report deadline open. The rationale measures through transmission of the line feed while OP-SYS-007 still records the choice between transmission start and completion.
findings.requested_change: State the approved observable transmission endpoint and apply it in each dependent test.

findings.description: The flow-fault entity is the affected task. One CON-SUP-104 evaluation can find several missing or out-of-order checkpoints, and CON-SUP-112 provides no selection rule for the task name in that case.
findings.requested_change: Specify which entity or entities the controller reports when one flow evaluation finds multiple bad checkpoints.

findings.description: When equally timed detections straddle the eight-report cutoff, either tied report can be displaced. CON-SUP-113 fixes the returned count and leaves that tie open.
findings.requested_change: Apply the approved ordering for equal detection times and cover a tie across the eighth-report cutoff.

findings.description: The CON-SUP-110 latch rule still leaves the effect of an intervening watchdog or other reset undefined. The rationale describes operation after startup checks, while the requirement gives no precise event that starts the 60 s fault-free interval.
findings.requested_change: Define the reset events that break the sequence and the observable start and end events for the 60 s interval.

findings.description: CON-SUP-104 and CON-SUP-105 place flow evaluation at cycle end. The revised item handles a skipped release, but a checkpoint received exactly at cycle end still has no verdict until OP-SYS-036 determines receipt and evaluation precedence.
findings.requested_change: Apply the approved precedence to coincident receipt and specify how verification establishes coincidence.

findings.description: A preempted task can use less processor time than its CON-SUP-103 limit while exceeding the same limit in elapsed time. The no-overrun decision depends on the execution-time measure still open in OP-SYS-013.
findings.requested_change: Reference the approved execution-time measure and exercise a preempted release that separates the two possible verdicts.

findings.description: SYS-TEST-014 now requires a complete STS frame and its rationale times the end of that frame from the last request character. OP-SYS-007 leaves both CON-SUP-113 measurement events open. A frame beginning before the deadline and ending after it can produce different verdicts.
findings.requested_change: Use the same approved request and response timing events as SYS-DIAG-007 and state the demonstration's deadline against those events.

findings.description: SYS-DIAG-003 assigns code 8 to watchdog resets and SYS-DIAG-002 requires an entity for each report. The allowed task, CODE and CONFIG values in CON-SUP-112 give no watchdog-reset entity.
findings.requested_change: Specify the approved entity for code 8 and cover it in the watchdog-reset report test.

findings.description: The GET FAULTS trigger applies whenever a request is received. A CON-SUP-110 reset can interrupt a pending response, and the set leaves acceptance and reply behavior in the retained safe state open.
findings.requested_change: Define request acceptance and response disposition before a pending reset, during recovery and while the safe state is latched.

findings.description: The first transmitted bit supplies the only history-entry deadline. If a watchdog reset prevents transmission from starting, that event never occurs. CON-SUP-110 requires retained history across watchdog reset, and OP-SYS-015 leaves the status of the detected fault open.
findings.requested_change: Specify the entry or recovery outcome when reset preempts the first bit, and verify the first GET FAULTS response after the restart.

findings.description: The less-than-100 ms refresh obligation applies whenever no listed task fault has become detectable since reset. This includes startup and retained-latch operation, where CON-SUP-106 leaves the independent-watchdog service policy open.
findings.requested_change: State the modes in which refresh is required and identify the reference event and bound for the first refresh in each applicable mode.

findings.description: The revised watchdog timeout criterion measures from the previous refresh. It gives no reference if the window watchdog is active and its first refresh never occurs, a case relevant to the fallback reset in STK-SUP-005.
findings.requested_change: Apply the approved activation and first-refresh policy and specify the required reset outcome if the first refresh is absent.

findings.description: CON-SUP-115 requires rejection of an unknown task. CON-SUP-101 names the default tasks but leaves the full supported identifier set open. A test cannot independently determine the verdict for an identifier outside the defaults.
findings.requested_change: Reference the approved supported identifier set and use it to establish known and unknown input cases.

findings.description: CON-SUP-113 supplies the STS template. Request framing, permitted state values and the meaning of fault count remain open, so a verifier cannot form a complete request and predict its response for a known state and fault history.
findings.requested_change: Use the approved request framing, state values and fault-count definition to specify complete request and expected-response examples.

findings.description: The 50 ms deadline in CON-SUP-113 gives no agreed measurement events for receipt and transmission. A reply that starts within 50 ms and finishes later has no unique verdict.
findings.requested_change: Identify the approved request-side and response-side events and use them for the timing test.

findings.description: The CON-SUP-113 GET FAULTS response lacks agreed wire order and completion framing. A verifier cannot distinguish a complete response with fewer than eight reports, including an empty history, from an incomplete transmission.
findings.requested_change: Define report order, response framing and complete encodings for empty, partial and full histories.

findings.description: CON-SUP-113 gives a 50 ms limit without agreed measurement events for receiving GET FAULTS and transmitting its multi-record reply. A reply can start within the limit and finish outside it.
findings.requested_change: Specify the approved timing events for the request and its reply, including a reply with zero records.

findings.description: CON-SUP-113 requires ERR for other requests. The requirement gives neither an approved recognition boundary nor a finite observation limit for the response. A test cannot establish when a complete unknown request was received or when a missing ERR fails.
findings.requested_change: Specify the approved recognition boundary and ERR response bound, and give verification cases for a complete unknown request and an incomplete request.

findings.description: STK-SUP-007 and CON-SUP-107 identify the image and when to check it. The integrity criterion and reference are still open, leaving the test without an independent accept-or-reject verdict for a given image.
findings.requested_change: Reference the approved integrity criterion and independently reproducible valid and invalid image fixtures.

findings.description: CON-SUP-107 and SYS-MEM-002 provide the CRC-32 polynomial. Different initial values, reflection settings or final XOR values can yield different CRCs for the same covered bytes.
findings.requested_change: Reference the approved CRC parameter set and supply a known-answer check for the defined configuration-block encoding.

findings.description: CON-SUP-114 requires measurement at the configured core clock. The requirement supplies neither the clock setting nor a controlled simulator configuration that identifies it, leaving the measurement conditions unreproducible.
findings.requested_change: Reference the approved clock setting or the controlled simulator configuration that supplies it.

findings.description: The test sets reset flags and checks that classification follows the flags. CON-SUP-111 names five classes, and the expected classification for combined or retained flags remains open.
findings.requested_change: Reference the approved mapping and flag precedence, and test the expected class for each relevant single, combined and retained flag pattern.

findings.description: CON-SUP-111 requires a startup message carrying the classified reset cause. Without approved framing and encoding, the verifier cannot identify the message or decode the cause.
findings.requested_change: Reference the approved startup frame and the encoding of each reset class.

findings.description: The stated test must establish that both outputs are low from any reset under CON-SUP-109. CON-SUP-003 and CON-SUP-005 give no evidence that the simulator represents external output levels during reset assertion and before GPIO configuration.
findings.requested_change: Establish evidence for the external levels on each reset path and use a verification method that covers reset assertion, early startup and the software-controlled interval.

findings.description: CON-SUP-109 requires status low from any reset, including one taken while SYS-SAFE-006 has status high. The test lacks evidence of the external pin level during reset assertion and before software acts.
findings.requested_change: Verify the external level from reset assertion, including a reset from high status, using approved pin behavior and evidence for each reset path.

findings.description: The startup fault test checks that neither output is high at any recorded sample. A trace starting after software begins can miss the reset interval and early transitions that the continuous CON-SUP-109 hold covers.
findings.requested_change: Cover the preceding reset and early startup with approved pin-level evidence, and use transition evidence to verify the uninterrupted hold for each startup fault.

findings.description: The sampled status trace can show low at fault injection while missing a high level during the preceding reset or before the first sample. SYS-SAFE-008 and CON-SUP-109 require the uninterrupted interval from reset.
findings.requested_change: Combine approved reset-interval evidence with status-transition observation through the fault and subsequent reset.

findings.description: The startup demonstration checks for the SYS-RST-009 message. Because CON-SUP-111 leaves the frame identity open, its presence cannot be distinguished from an FLT line or other simulated startup output.
findings.requested_change: Identify the expected startup frame in the demonstration using the approved message format.

findings.description: The isolated CON-SUP-107 code-integrity demonstration requires a complete code 5 report. If the computation never finishes and no report or reset occurs, the fallback observation limit still depends on an undefined startup duration.
findings.requested_change: Give the demonstration a finite failure point from an observable startup event, including a run with no computation completion, report or reset.

findings.description: The isolated CON-SUP-107 configuration-integrity demonstration requires a complete code 6 report. A run whose CRC check never finishes and produces no report or reset still has no defined observation limit.
findings.requested_change: Use an approved startup observation bound that yields a failure verdict when the CRC computation never finishes.

findings.description: The CON-SUP-115 range-fault test ends relative to the fault's detectability or an undefined fallback startup limit. When the range check never runs, its detectability event never occurs and absence of code 9 has no finite failure point.
findings.requested_change: Set a finite observation limit from startup that applies even if the range check never runs.

findings.description: If a watchdog is active during the CON-SUP-107 startup checks, the time remaining after a failing computation can be too short for the CON-SUP-110 report and software reset sequence. The startup watchdog policy and timing evidence remain open.
findings.requested_change: Establish the remaining watchdog time for each startup failure path and state the required outcome if it cannot accommodate reporting and software reset.

findings.description: The startup ordering applies when the failed check leads to a software reset request. A watchdog active during startup can reset the controller after the failed computation and before the report starts. CON-SUP-106 and CON-SUP-107 provide no timing basis that excludes this path.
findings.requested_change: Define the approved report and reset outcome for a startup failure preempted by a watchdog, and verify that sequence.

findings.description: The continuous latched hold under CON-SUP-109 and CON-SUP-110 includes reset assertion and the interval before software acts. CON-SUP-003 gives no pin or board evidence that both outputs stay driven low during those intervals.
findings.requested_change: Establish the hardware mechanism and evidence that maintain both external levels through each reset in the latched state.

findings.description: The latched status hold spans every intervening reset. CON-SUP-003 gives no external status-pin behavior during reset or before GPIO setup. A simulator trace with no high sample cannot establish the continuous hold required by CON-SUP-109 and CON-SUP-110.
findings.requested_change: Establish the pin behavior and a verification method that covers assertion and early startup on each latched reset path.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-003 requires fault declaration at the exact CON-SUP-103 execution-limit expiry. Its rationale says exact declaration is infeasible and its test allows a tolerance awaiting approval. The 100 µs measurement resolution supplies no declaration tolerance.
findings.requested_change: Align the declaration bound and the verification tolerance with the approved latency from expiry.

findings.description: SYS-DIAG-002 requires a CON-SUP-112 report for every detected fault. Refresh cessation under SYS-WDG-007 can trigger the CON-SUP-106 reset before transmission starts or completes. The report outcome under that preemption remains open.
findings.requested_change: Apply the approved reset precedence to the report deadline and define the outcome when transmission is cut off or never starts.

findings.description: SYS-DIAG-006 requires each detected fault to appear in history while fewer than eight faults have occurred. SYS-DIAG-010 permits entry by the first transmitted bit. A query or reset between detection and entry has different allowed histories under those rules and CON-SUP-110 and CON-SUP-113.
findings.requested_change: Define one approved point at which a report becomes part of the observable and reset-surviving history. Align the membership and entry requirements with it.
