findings.description: From the eighth detection onward, SYS-DIAG-011 changes required history membership at detection. SYS-DIAG-010 permits later entry. A GET FAULTS query or reset in that interval leaves the new report and any displaced report unresolved under CON-SUP-110 and CON-SUP-113.
findings.requested_change: Define the approved transition for adding the new report and removing the displaced report, including the result of reading or resetting during the transition.

findings.description: A flow fault at the end of a nominal 10 ms cycle can suppress the refresh with about 2 ms remaining before the CON-SUP-106 window expires. A hardware reset can then preempt the CON-SUP-110 software reset request and keep the incident out of the supervisor-reset latch count.
findings.requested_change: State the approved reset precedence and the effect on latch counting when a watchdog expires during the fault reaction sequence.

findings.description: CON-SUP-110 orders safe-state entry before report transmission. With refresh withheld under SYS-WDG-007, a CON-SUP-106 reset can preempt safe-state entry or transmission start. The requirement gives no outcome for that path.
findings.requested_change: Define the approved output and reporting outcomes across a watchdog reset that preempts safe-state entry or the start of transmission.

findings.description: CON-SUP-111 requires the service tool to read the latest reset cause. Neither CON-SUP-113 response includes it and other requests receive ERR. The approved interaction that satisfies both decisions remains open.
findings.requested_change: Identify the approved service-tool interaction and reconcile its framing and availability with CON-SUP-113.

findings.description: SYS-RST-013 requires transmission through the terminating line feed before the software reset request. A CON-SUP-106 watchdog reset can interrupt the report before the request, leaving the conditional ordering satisfied while the CON-SUP-110 and CON-SUP-112 report remains incomplete.
findings.requested_change: Define the required report completion or recovery behavior when a watchdog reset precedes the software reset request.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-003 declares overrun when execution is incomplete at expiry. SYS-SUP-007 forbids it for a completion measured at or below the limit. Under a mapping still allowed by OP-SYS-027, a completion shortly after expiry can satisfy both predicates.
findings.requested_change: Use one approved boundary rule for expiry, quantization and completion so the two requirements give the same verdict around the limit.

findings.description: The watchdog cutoff uses physical start-limit expiry for a late release. SYS-SUP-002 classifies lateness when the measured delay first exceeds the limit. If a refresh falls between those events, its eligibility can depend on whether the task subsequently starts before the measured crossing.
findings.requested_change: Use a cutoff the controller can determine at refresh time, aligned with the approved timing comparison. Test the interval between physical expiry and the measured crossing if one remains.

findings.description: SYS-WDG-005 now governs the independent watchdog only. A task fault can become detectable near that watchdog's 100 ms expiry under SYS-WDG-001 and CON-SUP-106. Withholding refresh can then cause a hardware reset ahead of the CON-SUP-110 report and software reset.
findings.requested_change: Apply the approved reset precedence to independent-watchdog expiry and cover a fault detected near that expiry.

findings.description: The inclusive refresh prohibition can cause a CON-SUP-106 window-watchdog reset before the CON-SUP-110 report and software reset request. That reset can interrupt the report and is classified separately from the same-code supervisor resets that drive the latch.
findings.requested_change: Apply the approved precedence to refresh cessation, report completion, reset-cause classification and same-code latch counting.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-001 and SYS-SUP-005 use the configured release schedule, but SYS-CFG-001 leaves the effect of changed periods on the CON-SUP-006 scheduler open. The rationale also defines release every n-th cycle by dividing the configured period by 10 ms, without an approved rule for periods that are not integer multiples of 10 ms.
findings.requested_change: Specify the supported periods, how they map to release cycles, and whether the scheduler uses them or rejects configurations that disagree with its schedule.

findings.description: A configuration block can fail its CON-SUP-107 CRC check and contain a value outside the CON-SUP-115 range. SYS-RST-012 requires a software reset for the integrity failure and SYS-RST-003 requires a latch for the range failure. The set leaves the validity and precedence of the two checks undecided.
findings.requested_change: Specify which checks are valid on a failing block, which reset or latch outcome takes precedence, and which fault reports are retained and transmitted.

findings.description: After a retained CON-SUP-110 latch and successful startup checks, SYS-SAFE-010 and SYS-SAFE-011 keep the signals low. SYS-MEM-004, SYS-SUP-001 and SYS-MEM-005 through SYS-MEM-008 lack a common rule for application releases, task supervision and run-time integrity checking in that state.
findings.requested_change: Define which functions run after successful startup with a retained latch and apply the same mode conditions throughout the set.

findings.description: SYS-RST-004 assigns the reset the code of the fault that starts the SYS-RST-001 deadline or triggers SYS-RST-012. Its rationale identifies this as an unapproved interpretation of CON-SUP-110. When faults with different codes precede one reset, that attribution changes the latch count on the next startup.
findings.requested_change: Approve the rule that attributes a fault code to a supervisor reset when multiple faults precede it and align the mixed-code latch tests with that rule.

findings.description: Startup messages, fault reports and service replies share the CON-SUP-007 serial line. The OP-SYS-042 estimate shows that an eight-report GET FAULTS response can occupy it longer than the CON-SUP-112 fault-report budget. The set still leaves frame handling, concurrent report limits and service deadline precedence open.
findings.requested_change: Define admitted traffic, frame handling and deadline precedence. Check the resulting timing against the approved frame lengths and maximum pending reports.

findings.description: The producer of the CON-SUP-107 block and the SYS-MEM-002 checker can use identical CRC parameters and disagree if they serialize fields differently or cover different bytes. The configuration producer and checker have no approved contract for those choices.
findings.requested_change: Specify serialization, the covered byte range, and the placement and treatment of the stored CRC field. Provide reference blocks with expected CRC values.

findings.description: The SYS-SAFE-007 and SYS-SAFE-008 rationales point to SYS-SAFE-003 for the CON-SUP-110 and CON-SUP-115 latched holds, which belong to SYS-SAFE-010 and SYS-SAFE-011. SYS-RST-012 points to SYS-RST-002 for report-before-reset ordering, which belongs to SYS-RST-013. SYS-RST-013 points to SYS-WDG-005 for window-watchdog cessation, which belongs to SYS-WDG-007.
findings.requested_change: Correct the rationale references to the requirements that own the latched holds, report-before-reset order, and window-watchdog refresh prohibition.

findings.description: The revised text gives the first CON-SUP-106 window-watchdog refresh a separate branch, but that branch requires bounds and a reference instant. Its rationale and OP-SYS-010 also admit an exemption from first-refresh spacing. Under that outcome, the text and the verification rationale cannot give the same verdict.
findings.requested_change: Make the first-refresh branch cover both a policy with spacing bounds and a policy that exempts the first refresh from spacing. Keep cycle association, watchdog enablement and flow-check ordering criteria applicable in both cases.

findings.description: The SYS-SUP-007 rationale cites SYS-SUP-004 as the requirement implementing the CON-SUP-103 execution-time measurement resolution. SYS-SUP-004 covers start delay, while the normative text of SYS-SUP-007 correctly refers to SYS-SUP-008 for execution time.
findings.requested_change: Point the execution-time measurement rationale to SYS-SUP-008.

findings.description: OP-SYS-043 proposes evidence methods for CON-SUP-110 retention. The target and Renode reset behavior, startup handling of retained state, and the validity of latch, history and reset-sequence records after an interrupted update still lack evidence or an agreed recovery rule.
findings.requested_change: Obtain approved target and simulator evidence for retention and define the startup recovery outcome for each interrupted update.

findings.description: SYS-TEST-011 fails a start after the configured limit by comparing the observed release and start instants. SYS-SUP-002 and SYS-SUP-006 use a measured start delay at CON-SUP-103 resolution. With truncation, for example, a 2.05 ms start against a 2 ms limit can fail the demonstration while satisfying the supervision rule.
findings.requested_change: Give the demonstration the same start-limit basis and boundary verdict as the approved timing supervision rule, or explicitly obtain approval for a distinct demonstration criterion.

findings.description: The SYS-TEST-014 rationale assumes that sending GET STATUS from 11.02 s preserves the normal-operation conditions of the other demonstrations. In the same run, SYS-TEST-011 can still be observing a release near the end of the window, and SYS-TEST-013 can still be waiting for the next independent-watchdog refresh. Service traffic can affect those observations.
findings.requested_change: Define when the same-run GET STATUS request can start relative to the final task and watchdog observations, and align the run schedule and acceptance criteria.

findings.description: The proposed test withholds T_IN completions from alive supervision while timing and flow supervision still see normal execution. CON-SUP-116 requires fault-injection hooks, and the proposed isolating stimulus still awaits approval. Without an admitted stimulus, SYS-TEST-006 lacks its specified positive control.
findings.requested_change: Approve an isolating alive-fault stimulus that preserves the timing and flow inputs, or revise the positive control and its dependent criteria.

findings.description: CON-SUP-112 specifies milliseconds since start. SYS-DIAG-005 selects the latest reset and refers to when the controller started, without identifying an observable reference event. OP-SYS-007 leaves that origin undecided.
findings.requested_change: Approve the observable event that starts the timestamp clock and apply it in the requirement and expected wire values.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-001 excludes a period if its control cycle starts before the checks pass. CON-SUP-107 bars early release but does not rule out a scheduled release later in that same cycle. CON-SUP-101 and CON-SUP-102 leave that alignment and the first T_DIAG release phase open.
findings.requested_change: Specify the first counted period of each task, including a release after the checks pass in a cycle already in progress and the initial T_DIAG phase.

findings.description: With truncation, a start 2.05 ms after release can measure 2.0 ms and satisfy SYS-SUP-006 against a 2 ms limit. CON-SUP-103 defines a start later than its limit as late. The mapping from true delays to measurements remains open.
findings.requested_change: Approve the measurement mapping and alignment and specify test verdicts just below, at and just above the limit.

findings.description: SYS-TEST-005 sets an 11 s continuous high-status interval from the status edge. CON-SUP-108 supplies 11 s for a full run-time integrity pass with a different origin. STK-SUP-015 and CON-SUP-116 supply no high-status demonstration duration.
findings.requested_change: Approve or replace the demonstration duration and its start event, then apply the decision to the dependent tests.

findings.description: The minimum of 1099 complete cycles assumes the first cycle starts no later than 10 ms after the status edge. CON-SUP-101 specifies a cycle duration and CON-SUP-109 specifies the status signal without bounding the interval between those events.
findings.requested_change: Approve the relationship between the status edge and the first cycle, or replace the fixed count with a criterion that follows from the approved cycle and observation rules.

findings.description: CON-SUP-112 gives a 10 ms deadline. The rationale times through completion of the terminating line feed, while OP-SYS-007 leaves the choice between start and completion of transmission undecided.
findings.requested_change: Approve the observable end event for the 10 ms interval and use it consistently in the report requirement and tests.

findings.description: The flow-fault entity is the affected task. One CON-SUP-104 evaluation can find several missing or out-of-order checkpoints, and CON-SUP-112 does not determine which task name appears or whether multiple reports result.
findings.requested_change: Specify the entity and report count for a cycle with multiple invalid checkpoints.

findings.description: When simultaneous detections straddle the eight-report cutoff, either tied report could be displaced. CON-SUP-113 gives the count and leaves the tie undecided, which changes the GET FAULTS result.
findings.requested_change: Specify a deterministic tie rule and check it with a history in which the tied reports straddle the cutoff.

findings.description: The CON-SUP-110 same-code latch rule still leaves the effect of an intervening watchdog or other reset open. The rationale describes fault-free operation after startup checks, while the requirement supplies no precise event that starts the 60 s interval.
findings.requested_change: Define which intervening resets break the sequence and which observable event starts the 60 s interval.

findings.description: CON-SUP-104 and CON-SUP-105 put flow evaluation and the fault event at cycle end. A checkpoint received at that same instant still has no unique verdict until receipt and evaluation precedence is decided.
findings.requested_change: Approve the precedence for a coincident receipt and specify the verification time base for deciding coincidence.

findings.description: A preempted task can use less processor time than its CON-SUP-103 limit while exceeding the same limit in elapsed time. SYS-SUP-007 gives a different no-overrun verdict depending on which basis is approved.
findings.requested_change: Approve the execution-time basis and include a preempted release whose verdict distinguishes the two measures.

findings.description: The revised demonstration measures a complete STS frame from the end of the request. The CON-SUP-113 deadline endpoints remain open in OP-SYS-007. A frame starting before 50 ms and completing afterward can therefore receive different verdicts.
findings.requested_change: Use the approved service timing events and specify the expected result for a response spanning the deadline.

findings.description: SYS-DIAG-003 assigns code 8 to watchdog resets and SYS-DIAG-002 requires an entity. The task, CODE and CONFIG values in CON-SUP-112 give no entity for code 8.
findings.requested_change: Approve an entity value for code 8 and apply it to the report format and verification.

findings.description: The GET FAULTS trigger applies whenever a request is received. A CON-SUP-110 reset can interrupt a pending reply, and the set leaves request acceptance and reply behavior while the safe state is latched open.
findings.requested_change: Define service behavior during safe-state entry, pending reset and latched operation, including requests accepted before a reset.

findings.description: The first transmitted bit supplies the only history-entry deadline. If a watchdog reset prevents transmission from starting, that event never occurs. CON-SUP-110 requires retained history across watchdog resets, and the outcome of the detected fault is open.
findings.requested_change: Specify whether and when the detected fault must become durable when a reset prevents transmission from starting.

findings.description: The less-than-100 ms refresh rule applies while no listed task fault has become detectable since reset. This includes startup and retained-latch operation, for which CON-SUP-106 supplies no independent-watchdog service policy or first-interval reference.
findings.requested_change: Define when independent-watchdog servicing is required in each mode and the event from which the first service interval is measured.

findings.description: The window-watchdog timeout is measured from the previous refresh. If the watchdog becomes active and its first refresh never occurs, that reference is absent. This case affects the fallback reset required by STK-SUP-005.
findings.requested_change: Specify the timeout reference and required outcome if an enabled window watchdog receives no first refresh.

findings.description: CON-SUP-115 requires rejection of unknown tasks. CON-SUP-101 names the default supervised tasks, and the approved supported identifier set is undefined. A verifier cannot determine the expected verdict for an identifier outside the defaults.
findings.requested_change: Identify the approved supported identifiers and their controlled source, then test identifiers inside and outside that set.

findings.description: CON-SUP-113 supplies the STS template. Request framing, permitted state values and the meaning of fault count remain open. A verifier cannot form a complete request and predict the response for a known state and history.
findings.requested_change: Approve request and response framing, the allowed state encodings, and the rules for calculating and encoding the fault count.

findings.description: The 50 ms deadline in CON-SUP-113 has no agreed receipt or transmission measurement events. A reply starting within 50 ms and finishing afterward has no unique timing verdict.
findings.requested_change: Define the observable start and end events for timing a GET STATUS response.

findings.description: The CON-SUP-113 GET FAULTS response lacks agreed wire order and completion framing. A verifier cannot distinguish a complete response with fewer than eight reports, including an empty history, from an incomplete transmission.
findings.requested_change: Specify record order and framing, including how zero through eight records and the end of the response are represented.

findings.description: CON-SUP-113 gives 50 ms without agreed measurement events for receiving GET FAULTS and transmitting its multi-record reply. A reply may start within the limit and finish outside it.
findings.requested_change: Define the observable start and end events, including the endpoint for multi-record and empty-history replies.

findings.description: CON-SUP-113 requires ERR for other requests. Without request framing and a finite observation limit, a verifier cannot determine when the controller has received a complete unknown request or when a missing ERR fails.
findings.requested_change: Approve the complete-request recognition rule and a finite ERR response observation criterion.

findings.description: STK-SUP-007 and CON-SUP-107 identify the image and when to check it. The integrity criterion and reference remain open, leaving the test without an independent accept-or-reject verdict for a given image.
findings.requested_change: Approve the integrity criterion and its reference, and identify test images with independently established expected outcomes.

findings.description: CON-SUP-107 and SYS-MEM-002 specify the CRC-32 polynomial. Different initialization, reflection and final XOR settings can yield different expected CRCs for the same covered bytes.
findings.requested_change: Approve the complete CRC parameter set and verify it against reference check values.

findings.description: CON-SUP-114 requires measurement at the configured core clock. SYS-RES-001 supplies neither the clock setting nor a controlled simulator configuration identifying it, leaving the processor-use measurement conditions unreproducible.
findings.requested_change: Identify the approved clock setting or controlled simulator configuration used for the processor-use measurement.

findings.description: The proposed test sets reset flags and checks that classification follows them. CON-SUP-111 names five classes but gives no expected classification for combined flags or flags retained from an earlier reset.
findings.requested_change: Approve a reset-flag mapping and precedence with expected results for single, combined and retained flags.

findings.description: CON-SUP-111 requires a startup message carrying the classified reset cause. The verifier has no approved framing or encoding for identifying the message and decoding the cause.
findings.requested_change: Approve observable startup-message framing and the encoding of each reset class.

findings.description: The test must establish that both outputs are driven low from any reset under CON-SUP-109. CON-SUP-003 and CON-SUP-005 do not establish that the simulator represents external output levels during reset assertion and before GPIO configuration.
findings.requested_change: Provide approved pin and board evidence and a verification method that covers both outputs through each required reset and early startup interval.

findings.description: CON-SUP-109 requires status low from any reset, including one taken while SYS-SAFE-006 has status high. The test lacks evidence of the external status-pin level during reset assertion and before software acts.
findings.requested_change: Establish how the external status level is verified from reset assertion through startup, including a reset initiated while it is high.

findings.description: The startup fault test checks that neither output is high at any recorded sample. A trace beginning after software starts, or missing transitions between samples, cannot establish the uninterrupted low interval from reset required by CON-SUP-109 and SYS-SAFE-007.
findings.requested_change: Combine reset-interval pin evidence with observation that can establish both outputs remain driven low through the entire required hold.

findings.description: A sampled trace can show status low at startup fault detection while missing a high level during reset or between samples. SYS-SAFE-008 and CON-SUP-109 require an uninterrupted low interval from reset.
findings.requested_change: Use evidence covering the external status signal during reset and startup, with observation that can detect any high transition in the required interval.

findings.description: The demonstration checks for the SYS-RST-009 startup message. With its CON-SUP-111 frame identity unresolved, the capture cannot distinguish it from a startup fault report or other serial output.
findings.requested_change: Use the approved startup frame and reset-cause encoding as exact recognition criteria in the demonstration.

findings.description: The isolated CON-SUP-107 code-integrity demonstration requires a complete code 5 report. If the computation never finishes and no report or reset occurs, the fallback observation limit depends on an undefined maximum startup duration.
findings.requested_change: Define a finite observation cutoff independent of successful completion of the failing computation.

findings.description: The isolated CON-SUP-107 configuration-integrity demonstration requires a complete code 6 report. A run whose CRC check never finishes and produces no report or reset still has no defined observation limit.
findings.requested_change: Define a finite observation cutoff for a run in which the CRC computation produces no observable outcome.

findings.description: The CON-SUP-115 range-fault test ends relative to detectability or an undefined startup limit. If the range check never runs, detectability never occurs and there is no finite failure point for absence of code 9.
findings.requested_change: Keep a finite cutoff from startup that applies even when the range-check event never occurs.

findings.description: If a watchdog is active during the CON-SUP-107 startup checks, the remaining time after a failed computation may be too short for the CON-SUP-110 report and software reset sequence. The startup watchdog policy and timing evidence remain open.
findings.requested_change: Establish the startup watchdog policy and show the report and reset sequence fits, or specify the approved preemption outcome.

findings.description: The ordering applies when the failed startup check causes a software reset request. A watchdog active under CON-SUP-106 can reset the controller after the CON-SUP-107 computation fails and before reporting or the software reset request. The set supplies no startup timing evidence that excludes that path.
findings.requested_change: Bound or disposition startup watchdog preemption between a failed computation and the ordered report and reset request.

findings.description: The latched hold under CON-SUP-109 and CON-SUP-110 includes reset assertion and the interval before software acts. CON-SUP-003 provides no pin or board evidence that both control outputs stay driven low throughout those intervals.
findings.requested_change: Establish that both outputs can remain driven low across the required resets and identify evidence that covers the entire latched hold.

findings.description: The latched status hold spans intervening resets. CON-SUP-003 provides no external status-pin behavior during reset or before GPIO setup, and a trace with no high sample cannot establish the continuous hold required under CON-SUP-109 and CON-SUP-110.
findings.requested_change: Establish the external status-pin behavior across the required resets and specify verification of the continuous latched hold.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-003 still requires declaration at the exact CON-SUP-103 execution-limit expiry. Its rationale says exact declaration is infeasible and uses a tolerance awaiting approval. The 100 µs measurement resolution supplies no declaration tolerance.
findings.requested_change: Approve a feasible bound from expiry to declaration and use it consistently in the requirement and verification.

findings.description: SYS-DIAG-002 requires a CON-SUP-112 report for every detected fault. Refresh cessation under SYS-WDG-007 can cause a CON-SUP-106 reset before transmission starts or completes. The required report outcome under preemption remains open.
findings.requested_change: Define the required outcome for the live report when a watchdog reset preempts its start or completion.

findings.description: While fewer than eight faults have occurred, SYS-DIAG-006 requires reports in history from detection. SYS-DIAG-010 permits entry by the first transmitted bit. A query or reset in between exposes different required histories under CON-SUP-110 and CON-SUP-113.
findings.requested_change: Use one approved entry and visibility rule for pending queries and for resets between detection and transmission.

findings.description: From the eighth detection onward, SYS-DIAG-011 changes required membership at detection. SYS-DIAG-010 permits later entry. A query or reset in that interval leaves the new report and any displaced report unresolved under CON-SUP-110 and CON-SUP-113.
findings.requested_change: Align history insertion and eviction with the approved entry event. Specify what survives or is visible before that event.

findings.description: At the end of a nominal 10 ms cycle with a flow fault, withholding the refresh can leave about 2 ms before the CON-SUP-106 upper window boundary. A hardware reset can preempt the CON-SUP-110 software reset request and keep the incident out of the supervisor-reset latch count.
findings.requested_change: Specify how watchdog preemption affects the required reset request and the same-code latch sequence.

findings.description: CON-SUP-110 orders safe-state entry before fault-report transmission. With a refresh withheld under SYS-WDG-007, a CON-SUP-106 reset can preempt safe-state entry or the start of transmission. SYS-RST-002 supplies no outcome for that path.
findings.requested_change: Specify the safe-state and reporting obligations when watchdog reset takes effect before either event.

findings.description: CON-SUP-111 requires the service tool to read the latest reset cause. Neither response in CON-SUP-113 includes it, and other requests receive ERR. An approved interaction satisfying both decisions is still missing.
findings.requested_change: Approve how the service tool obtains the latest reset cause and align the service interface and tests with that interaction.

findings.description: SYS-RST-013 requires transmission through the terminating line feed before the software reset request. A CON-SUP-106 watchdog reset can interrupt the report first, leaving the CON-SUP-110 and CON-SUP-112 report incomplete without a software reset request.
findings.requested_change: Define the required handling of incomplete transmission when watchdog reset takes effect before the report finishes.

findings.description: The refresh cutoff uses physical start-limit expiry for a late release; SYS-SUP-002 uses the first measured delay above the limit. If a refresh falls between those events, eligibility can depend on whether the task subsequently starts before the measured crossing.
findings.requested_change: Specify a cutoff that can be evaluated at refresh time and align it with the approved late-start measurement and classification rules.

findings.description: SYS-WDG-005 stops independent-watchdog service at the task-fault cutoff. If the fault becomes detectable near the 100 ms expiry under SYS-WDG-001 and CON-SUP-106, that watchdog can reset the controller before the CON-SUP-110 report and software reset request.
findings.requested_change: Make the precedence decision cover imminent independent-watchdog expiry and apply the result to reporting, reset outcome and the latch count.

findings.description: The inclusive refresh prohibition can cause a CON-SUP-106 window-watchdog reset before the CON-SUP-110 report and software reset request. The watchdog reset can interrupt the report and is classified separately from the supervisor resets used for the same-code latch.
findings.requested_change: Resolve window-watchdog precedence over the report and software reset sequence and state its effect on the latch criterion.
